articleTitle: An Orthogonal Dual-Polarization and Time Multiplexing Scheme of Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this article, we propose a time and orthogonal polarization division multiplexing scheme for local local oscillator continuous-variable quantum key distribution (LLO CV-QKD) system. According to the influence mechanism of time-domain diffusion and polarization disturbance on the key parameters, such as the channel transmittance and excess noise, of the studied system, we established a dual-polarization theoretical model and verified its validity by simulations. Here, the pulse width at the nanosecond level and polarization extinction ratio (PER) are considered for optimizing the performance of secure key rate (SIKR) quantitatively. For transmitting over 25 km optical fiber, the required PER should be above 22 dB when the pulse width is fixed to lns. Moreover, the optimal repetition frequency is obtained. In this case, 5.25 Mbps SKR can be achieved under the lns pulse width and 25dB PER, considering the $10^{11}$ finite-size block. Our work provides a systematic and theoretical framework for the study of improving the SKR of the dual-polarization CV-QKD system.

articleTitle: Metasurface-based On-board Optical Switching for Highly-Reliable Space Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Our Au metasurface has the stronger cosmic radiation resistance, and the more expeditious channel backup. To further enhance reliability of space communications, the neural network precisely controls the micro-displacement of chips for the metasurface backup.

articleTitle: Flexible Media Access Control Layer Key Technologies for Elastic Optical Access Network
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We first summary the elastic optical access network system architecture, Then the media access control layer key technologies include the advanced PHY independent and dependent MAC protocol, and the dynamic resource allocations are summarized.

articleTitle: Temperature Monitoring System for Underground Pipe Gallery Based on Power-Over-Fiber and Indoor Light Hybrid Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Based on the laser energy transmitted by optical fiber and indoor light energy, a hybrid energy harvesting system is proposed. The hybrid power supply cycle is 4 minutes shorter than the single-source power supply.

articleTitle: Analysis of influence factors in Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm for Solving Max-cut Problem
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In recent years, quantum algorithm research has developed rapidly, and it has become an important mode to use quantum computing cloud platform to carry out algorithm application exploration. Quantum approximate optimization algorithm can be used to solve the max-cut problem. In the process of algorithm execution, optimizer and various noise had obvious influence on the algorithm execution result. For the quantum computing simulator of HiQ platform, quantum approximate optimization algorithm was used for experimental verification, to study the types of optimizer, different noise scenarios, and the impact of noise error parameters on the maximum number of cutting edges. The prospect of quantum algorithm research was also discussed.

articleTitle: Spectrum Fragmentation Evaluation and Dynamic Bandwidth Allocation for Elastic Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes a spectrum resource evaluation mechanism and spectrum utility function in Elastic Optical Networks (EON). Using this function, the paper proposes an improved dynamic bandwidth allocation algorithm, effectively improving system transmission efficiency.

articleTitle: Multipoint and Multi-physical Quantity Sensing by Multimode Fiber with Demodulation of Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A multimode fiber (MMF) speckle sensor based on deep learning is demonstrated for sensing multi-physical quantity at different position. The mode fields at the end of MMF compose speckle patterns, which are sensitive to the various types of disturbing with different manners. Further, the MMF also carry numerous information, which make it possible sensing different physical quantity at different points in just one MMF. Here, it is demonstrated to sense stretching, bending, and temperature in a MMF of 0.5m by the deep learning methods. Its stretching precision is up to 0.005mm with the U-Net.

articleTitle: Temperature-insensitive sensor based on U-shaped few-mode fiber for blood glucose brix measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this study, a U-shaped few-mode fiber (FMF) sensor for blood glucose brix measurement is proposed, which is temperature-insensitive. These sensors with smaller bending diameters can be obtained by bending single-mode fiber (SMF)-FMF-SMF. The light leaks from fiber core to fiber cladding because the bending, which results in the occurrence of modal interference. The experiments show that the maximum blood glucose brix sensitivity is up to $1.081 \text{nm} / \%$ in the blood glucose brix range of 0%-18%, when the bending diameter is $\sim 1 \text{mm}$. And the sensors are temperature-insensitive in the temperature range of $10^{\circ} \text{C}-40^{\circ} \text{C}$. The sensor has advantages of compact structure and high sensitivity. Therefore, the sensor is suitable for applications in fields such as biomedicine.

articleTitle: Architecting Wavelength-Switched Optical Networks with Coherent P2MP Transceivers
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The recently presented coherent point-to-multipoint transceivers (P2MP-TRXs), which are enabled by digital subcarrier modulation, have been viewed as a promising substitute for the point-to-point transceivers, especially for the network segments with hub-and-spoke traffic patterns. This paper studies the network planning of wavelength-switched optical networks with P2MP-TRXs, which includes correlated routing and spectrum assignment, placement of P2MP-TRXs in groups and corresponding subcarrier assignments. We design an efficient heuristic to find near-optimal solutions in polynomial time.

articleTitle: Semiconductor Laser Chip Damage Detection Based on the Improved YOLOv8 Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We proposed an improved YOLOv8 algorithm and verified it through experiments. The results show that our proposed algorithm has $0.98 \mathrm{~ms}$ and $2.90 \%$ performance improvement on the average detection time and mAP@0.5:0.95, respectively.

articleTitle: All-optical format conversion from PDM-QPSK to PDM-PAM4 using vector phase-sensitive amplification
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, an all-optical format conversion system from polarization division multiplexed (PDM)-quadrature phase shift keying to PDM-4-level pulse amplitude modulation signal is proposed, analyzed and simulated. The method is based on the vector degenerate phase sensitive amplification (PSA) and non-degenerate PSA in semiconductor optical amplifiers (SOA). The constellations, eye diagrams, error vector magnitudes (EVM) and bit error ratios (BER) are measured to show the system performances.

articleTitle: Self-Adaptive Bandwidth Allocation to Address Dynamic Traffic Concept Drift in Optical Access Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this invited talk, we will review our recent work on online reinforcement learning-based dynamic bandwidth allocation (ORL-DBA) scheme that addresses concept drift in ML-enhanced optical access networks for supporting low-latency applications against network traffic dynamicity. The scheme improves bandwidth decisions via exploration or exploits existing decision knowledge to keep a low latency, with extensive simulations showing rapid and self-adaptive bandwidth decisions that yield up to 60% latency improvement in dynamic traffic environments.

articleTitle: Semantic Communication for Image Transmission in Intra-Datacenter Optical Interconnects
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A semantic communication system is proposed for massive high-definition image transmission in optical intra-connection links within the datacenter. Contrastive analysis shows that the proposed model can improve transmission capacity by more than two times.

articleTitle: Fiber Grating Sensing for Aerospace Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Fiber Bragg gratings having the advantages of lightweight, dielectric nature, immunity to electromagnetic interference, chemical passivity, and flexibility, integrated with being serially multiplexed with many sensors in a single fiber and multi-parameter sensing capability make them very competitive in aerospace applications. Research and development are carried out toward those of most interest to the industry.

articleTitle: Optimization design of FFE-DFE based on differential evolution algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose the p-ADE to optimize the tap coefficients of FFE-DFE in the IM/DD system. The results show that the convergence of p-ADE is faster than DE. The p-ADE provides similar SNR as LMS algorithm.

articleTitle: Fabrication of oriented nano-/meso-porous MOF thin films via fluid-assisted technique
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this work, we report our contributions in the field of fabrication of nano-/meso-porous MOF thin films. The orientation of MOF thin films is enhanced with the gravity assistance via fluid-assisted technology.

articleTitle: 100 Gbps Transmitter Based on Directly Modulated DFB Laser Array for DWDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We proposed and experimentally demonstrated a directly-modulated DFB laser array based on the reconstruction equivalent chirp (REC) technique with a transmission rate of 100 Gbps (10 channels * 10 Gbps). The proposed device is potential to be used in the DWDM systems.

articleTitle: Whispering gallery mode microsphere resonator integrated inside a capillary tube end
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a whispering gallery mode microsphere resonator, which is composed of single-mode fiber and capillary tube. The structure has the advantages of compact size and stable performance.

articleTitle: High-gain extended L-band EDFA with pre-amplified double-pass configuration
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An extended L-band EDFA with a pre-amplified double-pass configuration is demonstrated. The main amplifier contains an Er/Yb/P co-doped fiber pumped by two 1480 nm laser diodes. And the pre-amplifier is formed by a conventional erbium-doped fiber pumped by a 980 nm laser diode. The 20- and 30-dB gain bandwidths reach 65 nm (1556-1621 nm) and 58 nm (1558-1616 nm), respectively, with a maximum gain of 48.8 dB at 1566 nm and a gain of 20.1 dB at 1621 nm. The noise figure is 5.61±1.75 dB in the range of 1565-1610 nm. Besides, the saturated output power is up to 20.58 dBm tested at 1605 nm.

articleTitle: Reservoir Computing System Based on Polarization Dynamics of a Semiconductor Optical Amplifier Fiber Ring Laser
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: All-optical reservoir computing (RC) based on polarization dynamics of a unidirectional semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA) fiber ring laser is proposed and demonstrated experimentally. The SOA is used as a nonlinear node. The dynamical response in polarization of the ring laser is detected by a polarizer and a photodetector. The prediction error can be as low as 0.0762 for the Santa Fe time series prediction task, and the recognition accuracy can be as high as 100% for the signal classification task. The results show that the proposed RC has good prediction performance and strong classification ability. The polarization dynamics RC provides a new idea for the research of optical RC neural network and can be expected to process two tasks in parallel when the polarization dynamics and the intensity dynamics are used at the same time.

articleTitle: A Novel PAPR Reduction Scheme Using ISLM Cascading Neural Network-Based Companding Algorithm for CO-OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In coherent optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (CO-OFDM) systems, the high peak-average-power ratio (PAPR) is the major disadvantage that impacts the system performance, which is manifested in limiting the maximum power of lasers and exacerbating the fiber nonlinear effects. Therefore, a novel PAPR reduction scheme using improved selective mapping (ISLM) cascading neural network (NN)-based companding algorithm is proposed. Compared with the original OFDM and the single traditional scheme, the proposed scheme shows better PAPR reduction effect and bit error rate (BER) performance. Compared with the cascaded scheme, the proposed scheme has the similar effect but lower complexity.

articleTitle: Simulation and experiment of noise-like square pulses from a mode-locked erbium-doped fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper presents a numerical simulation and an experiment on the generation of Nosie like square pulses (NLSPs) in a long-cavity passively mode-locked fiber laser based on nonlinear optical loop mirror.

articleTitle: A novel gap compensation induced low-loss hollow-core anti-resonant fiber
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes a new structure of hollow-core anti-resonant fiber. The LP01 mode loss is reduced to 0.00602 dB/km by adding some gap compensation tubes. Furthermore, this value was reduced to 0.00103 dB/km through optimization.

articleTitle: CNN-based Methods of Traffic Matrix Prediction with Multiple Timesteps in Optical Network-on-Chip (ONoC)
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Optical Network-on-Chip (ONoC) is a promising type of interconnection with advantages such as high bandwidth and low latency. The network performance of ONoC can be further enhanced by accurate traffic matrix prediction. Convolutional neural network (CNN) can capture the spatial-temporal information of the input through convolution kernels. In this paper, three CNN-based methods (i.e., Multi-Width CNN, Multi-Channel CNN, and Multi-Input CNN) of traffic matrix prediction are proposed, with multiple timesteps. Multi-Width CNN and Multi-Channel CNN are Single-Input CNN. The evaluation results show that the traffic prediction accuracy of the Multi-Input CNN is significantly improved, compared to the single input. In addition, the Multi-Input CNN better improves performance of ONoC, compared to some popular neural network-based prediction methods.

articleTitle: Distributed Services Provisioning in an All-Optical Switching Based Edge Data Center Network
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Edge data centers (EDCs) efficiently serving latency-sensitive services and improving user experience are expected to be widely deployed in network edge. However, the conventional EDCs based on electric switches have bottlenecks in capacity, latency, and energy consumption due to the limit of Moore’s law. In this paper, we consider an all-optical switching-based EDC (AO-EDC) and address the distributed services provisioning problem in the context of an edge data center network (EDCN) made up of AO-EDC. Different service provisioning strategies, including network resource aware (NRA), computing power aware (CPA), and aggregated resource aware (ARA), are considered, respectively. Simulation results show that our proposed strategy can significantly improve the network performance in terms of overall task completion time (TCT) and load balance between different AOEDCs.

articleTitle: The Effect of Accompanied Optical Intensity Modulation on The Phase Noise in IFOS
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Phase Generated Carrier (PGC) is an important demodulation technique for the interferometric fiber optic sensors (IFOS). The minimum signal that the sensors can detect is determined by the noise floor of the system. So, it is of great importance to study the noise of IFOS. In this paper, the noise transfer model of PGC demodulation with light intensity disturbance is demonstrated and studied, and the theoretical simulation and experimental verification are carried out. The results show that the theoretical model can predict the experimental results well with the disturbance of light intensity, and can provide potential theoretical support for noise analysis and suppression of the system.

articleTitle: Spectral modeling and experimental validation of optical domain equalization for filtering mitigation
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An accurate model for optical domain equalization is proposed and verified with experiments. The modeled spectra fit well with measured curves, and prediction accuracy is better than 0.2 dB if used for filtering penalty estimation.

articleTitle: Regional Load-based Routing Optimization Algorithm for Satellite Network
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A load-balancing routing optimization algorithm for satellite networks based on regional load is proposed to address the problem of uneven link load in Low earth orbit satellite networks during data transmission.

articleTitle: A complex-valued NN equalizer based on pruning optimization algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a complex-valued NN equalizer based on iterative pruning algorithm is proposed and demonstrated in 64-QAM coherent optical detection. Compared with fully connected NN, the pruned sparse NN reduces computational complexity by ~55%.

articleTitle: Dual-Stage Gain-Clamped L-band Extended EYDFA with a Ring Cavity Laser
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A dual-stage gain-clamped L-band extended erbium-ytterbium co-doped fiber amplifier (EYDFA) is investigated. The gain of the EYDFA is clamped using a laser achieved by a ring cavity. The achieved 20-dB gain bandwidth is 47 nm (1568-1615 nm). A 24-dB (−34 to −10 dBm) gain clamped dynamic range is obtained at the maximum gain of 23.78 dB, with stability of ± 0.09 dB for signals at 1570 nm.

articleTitle: TFBG Humidity Sensor Based On Fullerene Derivative For Tachypnea Monitor
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes and experimentally demonstrates a fast response tilted fiber Bragg relative humidity sensor based on fullerene derivative, which is applied to monitor tachypnea.

articleTitle: Sensitivity optimization of fiber sensor based on two FBGs using microwave photonic interrogation technology
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Sensitivity optimization of fiber sensor based on two FBGs using microwave photonic interrogation technology is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. Two FBGs are attached on the upper and lower surfaces of a rectangular cantilever beam, which results in wavelength drift in opposite direction with external strain and same direction with temperature. As a result, the crosstalk caused by temperature is efficiently eliminated. The wavelength drift is converted into power variation of electrical signal by adopting the two taps microwave photonic filter response formed by two FBGs system. The effects of the modulation frequency and wavelength of the two FBGs on the system sensitivity are analyzed. In the experiment, the strain on two FBGs is demodulated by measuring the power of the recovered RF signal.

articleTitle: A fiber temperature sensor based on cascaded FBG and Sagnac interferometer with large measurement scale
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This article presents a fiber temperature sensor based on cascaded FBG and Sagnac interferometer. The sensor exhibits a temperature sensitivity of -1.357 nm/°C and a large measurement scale of 40°C to 80°C.

articleTitle: Optimization of Aperiodic Multi-Stage Amplification Transmission System for Low Overall DMG
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An all-fiber few-mode erbium-doped fiber amplifier (FM-EDFA) is built up for simulating an aperiodic multi-stage amplification and 3270km-long four mode transmission with the overall DMG of about 2 dB.

articleTitle: An Φ-OTDR event recognition method based on Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In recent years, CNN models have become a mainstream deep learning framework and have been widely used in research on improving the accuracy of $\Phi$-OTDR event recognition systems. However, a new deep learning framework, the Transformer model, has recently been proposed to replace CNN. In this article, an $\Phi$-OTDR event recognition method based on the transformer model is proposed. It has been compared with the CNN model, and experiments have shown that the transformer model performs better than CNN on pretrained models, with an accuracy rate of 99.64%. When the model is pruned to only 2 layers, its accuracy can still be saved, and the model size is reduced to 1.49M.

articleTitle: Tunneling Time: Ninety-Five Years
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Ninety-five-years lasting mystery of quantum-tunneling time had been solved essentially in 2022 based on a novel understanding of the tunneling mechanism. It would be technologically beneficial and even lead to amazing changes in fundamental physics.

articleTitle: Solving RCMSA in SDM-EON by using proximal policy optimization algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We use a new reinforce learning PPO algorithm to solve RCMSA. Simulation results show that using PPO algorithm can improve the efficiency of network spectrum resources and reduce the blocking rate of the requests.

articleTitle: Broadband Polarization-Insensitive Metalenses with High Focusing Efficiency Based on Inverse Design
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an broadband planar metalens that exhibits efficient operation within the wavelength range of 1270 to 2000nm and is insensitive to polarization. Compare with no metalens, the metalens can enhance the transmissivity of incident light by approximately 10%. In the operational wavelength range, the average focusing efficiency of the metalens is 56%, with a maximum focusing efficiency of 70.7%. And the average full width at half maximum (FWHM) of this structure is 0.5526µm. In the design process, we propose a new inverse design algorithm that is better suited for nanophotonic device design. The concept behind this new algorithm has significant implications for other inverse design algorithms.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Single- and Multiple- Eigenvalue based NFDM Optical Communication Systems with Discrete Spectrum Modulation
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In nonlinear frequency division multiplexing (NFDM) transmission system with discrete spectrum (DS) modulation, there are two methods to improve the data transmission rate, including the increase of the baud rate, and the number of multiplexed eigenvalues. Although some studies have been made on the DS-NFDM, the characteristic of these two manners have not been analyzed yet. Here, we give some analysis on the DS-NFDM system to improve the performances, including the spectral efficiency, noise robustness and bit-error-rate (BER) under the same data transmission rate. The simulation results show that the single-eigenvalue high baud rate scheme has advantages in spectral efficiency, but it is inferior to the multi-eigenvalue low baud rate one in terms of noise robustness and BER performance.

articleTitle: Continuous Two-Way Auction based Traffic Offloading in LEO Satellite Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a traffic offloading strategy based on continuous two-way auction to realize traffic transfer of the unbalanced feeder link in LEO satellite optical networks. Simulation results show that it can achieve less energy consumption.

articleTitle: Characterization of Pearls Using Spectroscopy Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To investigate the difference between freshwater cultured pearls and AKOYA pearls, we characterized the different types of pearls using Raman and Fluorescence spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Multidimensional Resource and Load Collaborative Scheduling Algorithm Based on Reinforcement Learning for Cloud Data Centers
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Task scheduling for multi-dimensional resources is one of the most fundamental problems in cloud data centers (DC). Among existing resolutions, the Q-learning model has been considered an excellent tool for fast task scheduling in DC environments. In this paper, we propose a load-balancing model for multi-dimensional resource scheduling in a cloud DC and a Q-learning based task scheduling algorithm (TSQL) that aims to reduce task makespan time and improve resource utilization. Simulation results show that, compared with existing algorithms, our algorithm optimizes 46.92%, 33.67% in makespan and resource utilization.

articleTitle: Performance improvement of multi-parameter measurement optical fiber sensors based on machine learning methods
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A machine learning based spectral data analysis method is proposed to solve the problem of limited measurement range of optical fiber sensors. This method expands the measurement range of the sensor and improves measurement accuracy.

articleTitle: Classification of plastics by near infrared spectroscopy based on clustering algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Studied a classification method of plastics by combining machine learning algorithm with near infrared spectral analysis technology. After SG filtering pretreatment and principal component analysis of spectral data, unsupervised clustering K-means algorithm, supervised clustering maximum likelihood estimation, Fisher discriminant and spectral Angle algorithm are used. PP, PET, HDPE, TPE, PLA, PBT, TPU, POM-M90, POM-GF20NC, TPB, PPS, ABS, PPO(natural), SAN, PPO(white), POM-F20 plastic particles were classified and discriminated. The classification results based on the near infrared spectral data of 16 kinds of plastic samples show that the K-means algorithm can distinguish POGF20NC, PLA and PPO from other plastic particles with the accuracy of 100%, 100% and80%, respectively. Fisher discriminant and maximum likelihood estimation method were used to identify POM-M90 and POM-F20 with an accuracy of 93%.The recognition accuracy of spectral Angle algorithm is 80% for PET, 47% for POM-F20, and more than 90% for other particles.

articleTitle: High precision optical fiber pressure sensor based on fused taper and small diameter fiber
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A fiber-capillary fusion coupling technology based on fused tapered is proposed, and fiber pressure sensor with high sensitivity, high resolution and low lag error is realized by using small diameter fiber and FBG temperature compensation. The developed sensor can measure extremely high temperature and pressure.

articleTitle: Bandwidth and wavelength tunable filter and its applications in fiber lasers
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A bandwidth and wavelength tunable filter and its application in fiber lasers are demonstrated. The continuous wavelength-tunable and the start-up and extinction dynamics of pulse in the Mamyshev oscillator have been studied with the filter.

articleTitle: Neural network-based FBG array sensor demodulation system with sparse data
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An efficient and practical neural network-based demodulation system for FBG array sensors is investigated, which fusing a augmentated algorthm so that system can achieve excellent interrogation precision under sparse data.

articleTitle: Distributed Forward Stimulated Brillouin Scattering Measurement on Polarization-Maintaining fiber with 80cm Spatial Resolution
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This article presents a novel distributed forward stimulated Brillouin scattering measurement scheme on polarization maintaining fiber (PM fiber) with a spatial resolution of 0.8 m named polarization separation assisted opto-mechanical time-domain analysis (PS-OMTDA). The activation pulse is injected into the fast axis and the probe pulse and probe wave is injected into the slow one, therefore, the acoustic wave is excited upon the fast axis but affected the probe wave on the slow axis. The backward Brillouin scattering of an activation pulse is effectively suppressed by isolating the acoustic activation and probing process. A spatial resolution of 80 cm is experimentally demonstrated over a PM fiber with a length of 34 m.

articleTitle: High performance reservoir computing system based on VCSELs with variable polarization information injection
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this work, we have demonstrated that, by introducing gradient boost technology, the parallel information processing performance can be improved in a reservoir computing (RC) system based on vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers (VCSELs) under variable polarization information injection (VPII). For the VPII scheme, the information is added into X-polarization component (X-PC) and Y-polarization component (Y-PC) of VCSEL simultaneously, and outputs from two PCs of VCSEL are utilized to construct the node matrix. Although such an information injection method can double the processing rate, the system performance needs to be further improved. In this work, the gradient boost technology is adopted to enhance the system performance, for which an extra VCSEL-based reservoir is added to correct the residual error of the original reservoir. Via parallel processing Santa-Fe chaotic time series prediction task (Stask) and waveform recognition task (Wtask), the effectiveness of adopting gradient boost technology to improve the performance of VCSEL-based RC is confirmed.

articleTitle: High-security chaotic dynamical enhanced strategy based on reservoir computing
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a high-security chaotic dynamical enhanced strategy based on a nonlinear dynamical enhanced chaotic system generated by reservoir computing (RC). The proposed system is applied to an orthogonal frequency division multiplexed passive optical network (OFDM-PON), which gets more complex chaotic behavior by using Sine-Henon cascade mapping (S-Henon). RC generates the chaotic sequences that are used to produce the masking vectors to encrypt the constellation and subcarriers, which can resist the degradation of chaotic dynamics.

articleTitle: Analysis of Sensing Characterictics of a Helical Long-Period Fiber Grating Written in a Graded-Index Few-Mode Fiber and its Temperature Sensor Application
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The unique sensing characteristics of a helical long-period fiber grating (HLFG) written in a graded-index few-mode fiber (GI-FMF) was analyzed in the paper. Simulation results show the dispersion factors of the designed HLFG can keep higher values in a wide wavelength rage than those of traditional fibers, resulting in the unique characteristics of the ultra-wide linear range and the ultra-high sensitivity for sensing temperature. Experimental results show the temperature sensitivity of $122.2 \ \mathrm{pm}/^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ can be obtained by using the designed HLFG, indicating the temperature sensing potential application of this device.

articleTitle: Trace Detection of Cadmium ion Based on Glutathione-Functionalized TFBG-SPR Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper presents a novel cadmium ion sensor that utilizes a tilted fiber Bragg grating functionalized by glutathione. Gold nanoparticles are used to amplify localized refractive index changes. The limit of detection is 0.07 nM.

articleTitle: Distributed temperature and strain discriminative sensing based on a bend-tolerant few-mode fiber with DPP-BOTDA
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We proposed a distributed temperature and strain discriminative sensor based on differential pulse-pair Brillouin optical time-domain analysis and bending-tolerant few-mode fiber. The discriminative deviation of 2.78°C and 33.2 µ$\varepsilon$ was demonstrated, respectively.

articleTitle: Reservoir computing system based on an optoelectronic oscillator with double delay feedback
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A time-delayed reservoir computing (RC) system based on an optoelectronic oscillator with double delay feedback is proposed. On the basis of a conventional RC system based on an optoelectronic oscillator, an optical delay feedback path is introduced, through which the output light of the system is fed back to the Mach-Zehnder modulator (MZM). A word error rate of 0 for signal waveform classification task and a normalized mean square error of 0.0097 for Santa Fe chaotic time series prediction task are obtained. The simulation results verify the prominent classification and prediction performances of the proposed RC system. The system is compact in structure and easy to implement.

articleTitle: Mid-infrared tunable interband cascade laser employing double-trench waveguide structure with a tuning range of 118 nm
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We present a widely tunable single-mode interband cascade laser (ICL) emitting at 3.3 μm based on the V-coupled cavity employing a double-trench structure, with aside-mode suppression ratio of up to 36 dB.

articleTitle: Mid-Infrared Ethane Detection System Based on TDLAS Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Ethane gas is an important raw material for production, and it is important to realize the detection of ethane gas. This paper introduces a mid-infrared ethane gas detection system: using direct absorption spectroscopy (DAS) and wavelength modulation spectroscopy (WMS) for the detection of ethane gas respectively. By standard deviation evaluation, the detection limits of DAS and WMS were 1.0167 ppm and 0.1076 ppm, respectively. The results of the detection show that the WMS has higher accuracy, better linearity, and greater reliability than the DAS. In contrast, the DAS has a lower system complexity and greater potential to reduce system volume.

articleTitle: Extrinsic Two-Photon Polymerization 3D Printed Fiber Fabry-Perot Air Cavity For Temperature Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A micro extrinsic Fabry-Perot air cavity is constructed on the fiber end using two-photon polymerization 3D printer. Experimental measurements show that the temperature sensitivity reaches 0.24 nm/°C in the temperature range of 20°C-60°C.

articleTitle: Measurement and Splicing Evaluation of a Low Crosstalk 4-core Fiber
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, the measurement and splicing of a weakly-coupled 4-core-fiber is reported. The customized splicing machine and upgraded algorithm are used to achieve the low splicing loss of the 4-core fiber. The average splicing loss of the fiber is 0.10dB. This paper firstly evaluate the influence of splicing to insertion loss and crosstalk. With ultra-low splicing loss and low extra crosstalk, this MCF can be used in long-haul weakly-coupled SDM systems that allows to multiply the capacity.

articleTitle: A Neural Networks Nonlinear equalizer based on Volterra Series Tranfer Function
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a nonlinear equalizer using neural networks based on Volterra series transfer function(VSTF). The input power was improved by 3dB. Compared to VSTF and DBP, the calculation complexity are reduced by 79.34% and 84.44%, respectively.

articleTitle: Defect Detection in Transparent Materials Based on Optical Coherence Tomography
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: High-precision optical components have put forward strict requirements for manufacturing technology, and quality detection technology. In this work optical coherence tomography is used to detect both surface and internal defects in transparent optical materials.

articleTitle: A fiber-optic Fabry-Perot acoustic sensor based on PDMS diaphragm
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes a low-cost detachable extrinsic Fabry-Perot (FP) acoustic pressure sensor (EFPAPS) based on a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) diaphragm. An FP microcavity with air as the medium is formed between the PDMS diaphragm and the fiber end face. The experimental results show that the fabricated sensor has a high optical contrast of approximately 7 dB, and its initial cavity length is $26.367 \mu m$. The minimum detectable sound pressure (MDP) at 100Hz and 420Hz are $14.826 \mu \mathrm{Pa} / \mathrm{Hz}^{1 / 2} \text{@} 100Hz$ and $26.9793 \mu \mathrm{Pa} / \mathrm{Hz}^{1 / 2} \text{@} 420Hz$ respectively. And The sound pressure sensitivities at these two frequencies are 2.5006 mV/Pa and 8.9524 mV/Pa respectively. The sensor’s high-precision measurement of medium and low-frequency sound waves and its simple preparation process make it expected to shine in the field of acoustic sensing.

articleTitle: A Fiber Optic Thermal Fabry-Perot Interferometer for the Detection of β-Carotene
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose an optical fiber Fabry-Perot interferometer (FPI) based on the photothermal effect to detect β-carotene. The sensor has potential applications in the field of environmental pollution detection.

articleTitle: Extraction of a single OFC mode based on the SBS effect and Injection locking
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We show how to extract a single mode from mode-locked lasers based on stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) and optical injection locking. The selected comb line with ultra-narrow linewidth and high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is experimentally achieved.

articleTitle: Dynamic distributed Brillouin optical fiber sensing with frequency-agile technique
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a scheme using the frequency-agile technique to measure Brillouin gain and loss spectra simultaneously to simplify the experimental equipment and improve the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the traditional Brillouin optical time-domain analysis (BOTDA) system. The pump wave is modulated into the double-sideband frequency-agile pump pulse train (DSFA-PPT), and the continuous probe wave is up-shifted by a fixed frequency value. With the frequency-scanning of DSFA-PPT, pump pulses at the −1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> order sideband and the +1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> order sideband interact with the continuous probe wave via stimulated Brillouin scattering, respectively. Their difference of the Brillouin loss and gain spectra relates to a synthetic Brillouin spectrum with a 3.65-dB SNR improvement for a 20ns pump pulse. This work simplifies the experimental device, and no optical filter is needed.

articleTitle: BER Performance Analysis of O-OFDM-IM System Under Non-ideal Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, the effects of atmospheric turbulence, aiming error, frequency offset, and channel estimation error on the communication performance of the optical OFDM-IM system are investigated, and an expression for the average BER of the optical OFDM-IM system under this non-ideal condition is derived. Finally, simulation experiments are used to verify the results. The results show that under the same conditions, the reliability of the system becomes less and less as the turbulence intensity, frequency offset, and channel estimation error increase.

articleTitle: Compact Low-Loss Dual-Mode Silicon Waveguide Bend with Simple Geometry
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A silicon waveguide bend with a width of 900nm and an effective radius of 3µm is proposed, which supports both TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> modes while maintaining low insertion loss and crosstalk. An adaptive particle swarm optimization algorithm is proposed for the bend waveguide design, enabling automated generation of optimal structures with minimal human intervention. The device is fabricated using electron beam lithography. The measured insertion losses for TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> modes are below 0.02 dB and 0.09 dB/90°, respectively, across the entire C-band. The measured inter-mode crosstalk is below −22.4dB per 90°.

articleTitle: 12.14Gb/s Si-substrated GaN/InGaN-based Micro-Photodetector Array With V-pit Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper we proposed a photodetector using GaN/InGaN-based multi-quantum well micro-LED fabricated on Si-substrate. It yields 12.14 Gb/s data rate in our experiment, which is the highest record for GaN-based micro-PD.

articleTitle: L-band extended EDFA co-pumped by backward ASE
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We employ the backward amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) co-pump technique in L-band extended erbium-doped fiber amplifier (LE-EDFA) for the first time. The gain is improved by $5.1 \sim 16.7$ dB in the wavelength range of $1570 \sim 1620$ nm when the pump power is 450 mW. A two-stage LE-EDFA co-pumped by backward ASE is then demonstrated with a 20dB gain bandwidth covering $1570 \sim 1610$ nm and the noise figure of less than 6 dB.

articleTitle: Ultrafast Compressive Sensing Imaging Using In-Fiber Grating
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An ultrafast compressive sensing imaging system is proposed using in-fiber grating. The in-fiber grating, namely 45° tilted fiber grating (TFG), acts as the in-fiber polarizer, and a lateral light diffraction device at the same time. Due to its polarization-sensitive feature, the 45° TFG along with the polarization modulator can perform the compressive sensing process. A state-of-art demonstration is performed based on the proposed imaging system and a field of view (FOV) of 2mm by 4mm and data compression ratios of 8% and 16% are achieved.

articleTitle: Driver-Free Net-422-Gbps/λ PAM transmission based on TFLN Modulator, Advanced DSP and single DAC with the Highest Net Information Rate in 400G/λ IM/DD
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report ultrahigh-speed transmission of net-422-Gbps/λ PAM-20 signals over 0.5-km SSMF in C-band, based on only one-DAC without any electrical amplifications, achieving a record net information rate (bits/symbol) in 400G/λ IM/DD.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of OPGW optical cable under simulated icing based on BOTDR
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper simulates and experiments the icing of optical cable based on Brillouin optical time-domain reflection technology. The results show that the ice-coating aggravates optical fiber strain to the point of rapid fiber rupture.

articleTitle: Online, Rapid Measurement of Pb²⁺ and Hg²⁺ Ions in Water Based on Quantum Dot Fluorescence Quenching Method
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel method and device for detecting heavy metal ions in water using the principle of quantum dot fluorescence quenching based on a 405nm semiconductor laser had been designed. This technique produced fluorescence-stimulated emission of heavy metals in water by combining interdisciplinary expertise from the fields of chemistry and optics. The detection was quick, easy, and capable of monitoring the level of heavy metal ions in water continuously online. The experimental results demonstrated that the Hg²⁺ concentration exhibited good linear relationships within the low range of 0.001-0.2 mg/L(R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>=0.998) and the high range of 0.2-2 mg/L(R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>=0.992). The Pb²⁺ concentration range of 0.0.005–5 mg/L also exhibited a strong linear association (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>=0.997). The online detection system for Hg²⁺ and Pb²⁺ responded within 60 seconds and demonstrated good short-term stability and repeatability, fulfilling the demands for quick detection.

articleTitle: Cost-efficient protocol upgrading for quantum key distribution over metro optical networks
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes a cost-efficient protocol upgrading algorithm for quantum key distribution over metro optical networks, reducing the number of channels added for QKD protocol upgrading by 17.6% compared to the benchmark.

articleTitle: Metasurface Technology and Device for Ultra Precision Optical Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Precision measurement is gradually shifting from laboratories to real-world environments and production platforms to meet the increasing requirement of intelligent manufacturing. Metasurfaces, 2D engineered artificial interfaces, have emerged as candidates to replace traditional refractive lenses.

articleTitle: Phase noise measurement of high-frequency microwaves based on electro-optical combs
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Assisted by optical injection locking (OIL) and dual-wavelength self-heterodyne techniques, we propose a method to achieve accurate phase noise measurements of high-frequency microwaves based on electro-optic combs.

articleTitle: Vortex mode generation and decomposition based on mode selective coupler
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a vortex mode formation with polarization control in a few-mode polarization-maintaining fiber. The proposed mode selective couplers act as efficient mode converters to produce spectrally insensitive high-order modes at the visible wavelengths.

articleTitle: Fiber optic temperature sensor based on Fabry-Perot microcavity structure
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We have developed a temperature sensor based on Fabry micro-cavity structure with the advantages of high sensitivity, corrosion resistance and high robustness.

articleTitle: All-fiber Fourth-order LP Mode Selective Excitation Employing a Mode Selective Photonic Lantern
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An all-fiber fourth-order LP mode converter is proposed and fabricated. The insertion loss of odd and even fourth-order LP mode is less than 0.2 dB and 0.4 dB at 14601640 nm, respectively.

articleTitle: A Conditional Generative Adversarial Network aided Few-mode Fiber Channel Modeling for large-capacity optical fiber communication
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a conditional generative adversarial network (CGAN) aided channel modeling technique is proposed for few-mode fiber (FMF) optical communication. Simulation results demonstrate the proposed CGAN-aided FMF modeling technique achieve an attractive effect on modelling accuracy.

articleTitle: Fiber Nonlinear Effects Compensation by Using Multi-Head Self-Attention Bi-LSTM
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A bi-directional long short-term memory neural network based nonlinear equalizer with multi-head self-attention mechanism is proposed. The Q-factors of single-channel and 5-channel 130Gbaud dual-polarization fiber-optics communication systems are improved by 0.75 dB and 0.68 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of an All-Fiber FM - EDFA by Optimizing the Bidirectional Pumping Configuration
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An all-fiber few-mode erbium-doped amplifier is designed and constructed under the bidirectional pumping configuration. The power ratio of forward and backward pump modes and the influence of different pump modes on the amplifier characteristics of the three signal modes are experimentally studied. The research shows that the amplifier presents good performances in the combination of forward LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> pump and backward LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> pump. The signal gain can be more than 22.5 dB, the mode gain difference less than 0.91 dB, and the noise figure of LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> signal mode can be reduced to 7.52 dB.

articleTitle: Performance of optical beam switching using liquid crystal polarization grating for FSO networks
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a non-mechanical optical beam control method based on liquid crystal polarization grating (LCPG). Four angular beam pointing and switching in the range of 12° can be realized by using two LCPGs.

articleTitle: High-Quality Bragg Gratings fabricated by Femtosecond Laser in Planar Lightwave Circuit Chip
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper utilizes femtosecond laser direct writing to fabricate high reflectivity and low insertion loss Bragg gratings in planar lightwave circuit chip.

articleTitle: A miniature structure based on ring-core fibers for temperature and strain sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The paper reports a novel fiber-optic sensor. It is consisted by the RCF embedded long period fiber grating and RCF-based Mach-Zehnder interferometer and has the ability of simultaneous measuring temperature and strain.

articleTitle: An All-optical plasmonic modulator based on graphene/black phosphorus heterostructure at visible wavelengths
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An all-optical plasmonic modulator working at visible wavelengths based on graphene/black phosphorus heterostructure is proposed. This modulator is capable of operating from $400 \mathrm{~nm}$ to $800 \mathrm{~nm}$ with large extinction ratio up to $55 \mathrm{~dB}$.

articleTitle: Geometric and Probabilistic Shaping of 16/32-QAM based on Swarm intelligence algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We design the hybrid PS/GS-16/32QAM based on intelligence algorithm in optical fiber transmission. The position and the probability of constellation points are jointly optimized. Results show that PS/GS-16/32QAM outperforms GS-16/32QAM and traditional 16/32QAM.

articleTitle: Secure OFDM Transmission with Integrated Physical-Layer Key Distribution using NOMA
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A secure OFDM data communication scheme is proposed for wireless or optical networks, where a 200Kbps data transmission integrated with 50Kbps physical-layer key distribution is demonstrated using non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA).

articleTitle: Generation of Noise-Like Square Pulses and Pulse Clusters from a Mode-Locked Erbium-Doped Fiber Laser
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Noise-like (NL) square pulses under different mode-locked conditions and pulse clusters with different numbers (2-12) of sub-pulses are generated from a passively mode-locked erbium-doped fiber laser based on nonlinear polarization rotation (NPR).

articleTitle: Temperature and strain monitoring system based on linear optical sampling
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The application of linear optical sampling to FBG sensing measurement can effectively overcome the limitation of traditional measurement methods in achieving precise measurement due to resolution constraints.

articleTitle: A Refractive Index Sensing System by Using EFPI Based Microwave Photonic Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a refractive index (RI) sensing system using an extrinsic Fabry-Perot interferometer (EFPI) structure based microwave photonic filter (MPF). Two EFPI sensors with cavity lengths of $500 \mu \mathrm{m}$ and $960 \mu \mathrm{m}$ have been fabricated, and the sensitivities of 627.953 MHz/RIU and 1201.653 MHz/RIU have been achieved, respectively. The proposed sensing system has the advantages such as high sensitivity, good linearity, and enlarged measurement range.

articleTitle: An Overlapped-Dense LSTM Neural Network for Nonlinear Optical Fiber Transmissions
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose an overlapped dense long short-term memory network (OD-LSTM) that consumes different hidden units at different time steps. We use it for effective fiber nonlinearity compensation with a lower complexity.

articleTitle: Distributed optical fiber sensing technology for wind turbine monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for wind turbine condition monitoring that combines a phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometer ($\varphi$-OTDR) with a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN). The $\varphi$-OTDR sensing fiber is laid on the three towers of the wind turbine to collect real-time operating status signals. The acquired signals are processed by the 1D-CNN to perform pattern recognition of the condition signals. Experimental results demonstrate that the recognition accuracy exceeds 95%, proving the effectiveness of our proposed approach.

articleTitle: Phase-sensitive Optical Time Domain Reflectometry Assisted by Image-Matching and Dual-frequency
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This article presents a novel phase-sensitive optical time domain reflectometry (Φ-OTDR) with a spatial resolution of 2-m on a 90-m fiber assisted by image-matching and dual-frequency. The temporal resolution was improved fourfold compared to the conventional Φ-OTDR based on the cross-covariance algorithm. Using the same temporal window, the measurement error was decreased from 21.4% to 1.2% in the distributed experiment, showing a considerable improvement in the measurement precision.

articleTitle: A real-time monitoring method for Brillouin fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a real-time monitoring method for Brillouin fiber laser. The Mach-Zehnder interferometer and the gas cell are introduced for frequency calibration to ensure the accuracy of spectroscopy data.

articleTitle: Statistical Properties of Modal Dispersion in Multiple-mode Fibers
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Using a statistical model based on the density-matrix formalism, we study the probability distribution and frequency diversity of modal dispersion in multiple-mode fibers. The results verify the validity and effectiveness of the density-matrix formalism.

articleTitle: Common-mode Noise Suppression of Interferometric Fiber Optic Hydrophone Based on High Frequency Heterodyne Detection and Phase Locking
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Accurate and reliable signal measurement is very important for fiber optic hydrophone sensing system. The optical fiber hydrophone is susceptible to common-mode noise (CMN) during the detection process, which may lead to distortion or error of the signal. By suppressing $C M N$, the signal-to-noise ratio of signal can be improved and the sensitivity of sensor can be improved. In this paper, a CMN suppression method for optical fiber hydrophone based on high frequency heterodyne demodulation and phase locking technology is proposed. The hydrophone signal is obtained by high frequency heterodyne demodulation technology, and the reference hydrophone is constructed by using $3 \times 2$ coupler. The initial phase of the output signal of the sensing interferometer and the reference interferometer is locked to realize the noise signal in-phase cancellation and greatly improve the CMN suppression level. The experimental results show that the method can suppress $C M N$ up to −29dB at 150Hz~1kHz. The correlation coefficient between the reference interferometer and the sensing interferometer output is increased by 44.9%, and its standard deviation is reduced by about 98%. When the signal is added to the system, the signal-to-noise ratio is increased by 10.9dB, which is of great significance for weak signal detection.

articleTitle: First over 100-Gb/s PAM-8 IM/DD Fiber Transmission System at 2-micron Waveband Enabled by Advanced DSP
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate the first over 100-Gbps PAM8 signal transmission in IM/DD system at the 2-micron waveband enabled by advanced DSP. Nonlinear FTN-type DSP algorithms are applied to overcome the nonlinear ISI impairments.

articleTitle: High Sensitivity, Multi-parameter Optical Probes Based on Reflective Fiber Couplers
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Multi-parameter optical sensor using optical probes based on reflective fiber coupler to detect the curvature, liquid level, temperature and refractive index. In addition, the multi-parameter sensor can realize the detection of damped vibration signal and sound recognition with high stability.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Multicarrier Modulation Waveforms for Terahertz Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper presents an experimental comparison among the orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), filter bank multicarrier (FBMC) and orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) waveforms in a terahertz photonic-wireless point-to-point communication system operating at 300GHz. Our results show that, all waveforms have similar peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR), the OTFS and OTFS waveforms can achieve comparable bit error rate (BER) performance, while the FBMC waveform outperforms in terms of the out-of-band decay at the cost of non-orthogonality between subcarriers, leading to the deterioration of BER performance at high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) region.

articleTitle: Relative intensity noise suppression based on saturabale gain in the erbium doped fiber amplifier
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose the suppression of relative intensity noise (RIN) of laser based on the saturable gain in the erbium-doped fiber amplifier. How the input power, pump power will influence the RIN suppression are theoretically studied.

articleTitle: Temperature Sensing through Imperfect Quarter-Waveplate in Fiber-Optic Current Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a method of temperature sensing in fiber-optic current sensor without additional temperature sensor, based on the retardation of the quarter-waveplate varying with the ambient temperature, which is helpful to temperature compensation of fiber-optic current sensor itself.

articleTitle: Highly Dispersive Fiber with Two Graded-Index Concentric Cores
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A highly dispersive fiber with two graded-index concentric cores is proposed with −34948 $\mathrm{ps} /(\mathrm{nm} \cdot \mathrm{km})$ chromatic dispersion at 1480nm. The influence of structural and material parameters on dispersion of the fundamental mode are further discussed.

articleTitle: Mutual influences of modal dispersion and mode-dependent loss in multiple-mode fibers
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We construct a statistical model of modal dispersion and mode-dependent loss based on the density-matrix formalism, and employ it to study the mutual influences of modal dispersion and mode-dependent loss in a 4-mode fiber.

articleTitle: Broadband Beam Control and Gain Enhancement Based on Non-Resonant Transmission Phase Gradient Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Conventional phase gradient metasurfaces suffers from disadvantage among unique or multi-working frequency. Hence, we propose a novel method to extend the broadband transmission phase gradient metasurfaces (TPGMs) using non-resonant modes. The TPGMs consists of periodic and multilayer subwavelength elements that contribute to a wide range of transmission phase shift. The simulation results show that proposed TPGMs present anomalous transmission phenomenon at 8 to 12 GHz, and a design example of antenna gain enhancement is given to prove the practicality of TPGMs.

articleTitle: Synthesis of narrow half-peak width green InP/ZnSeS/ZnS core/shell/shell quantum dots
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: InP based quantum dots are an excellent candidate for replacing Cd-based, Pb-based and other heavy metal quantum dots (QDs) in areas such as displays and solid state lighting. In this paper, we use a safer, more environment friendly and inexpensive aminophosphine as a phosphorus precursor and employ a simple one-pot method to synthesize InP based quantum dots. In particular, the synthesis of narrow full width at half maximum (FWHM 37 nm), bright and efficient green InP/ZnSeS/ZnS quantum dots was achieved by adjusting the thickness of ZnS layer.

articleTitle: Adaptive Channel Modeling with Conditional Generative Adversarial Network for 209-GHz Fiber-Terahertz Integrated Communication System
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and experimentally demonstrate an adaptive wave-to-wave level channel-modeling method based on conditional generative-adversarial-network (CGAN) for the 209-GHz fiber-THz integrated communication system, achieving lower BER fitting error and higher accuracy under different channel conditions.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis of Full-Bandwidth Statistical Properties in Raman Random Fiber Laser
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Raman random fiber laser (RRFL) involves complex physical processes. Here, we experimentally investigate full-bandwidth statistical properties of RRFL for the first time. The intensity probability density function of RRFL time-domain properties deviates from exponential distribution, indicating correlations exist between different frequency components of the spectrum.

articleTitle: Ti2C MXene-based highly sensitive optical fiber MZI salinity sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper presents an optical fiber MZI sensor based on Ti2C-MXene nanosheet, which has a salinity sensitivity of −3.4360 nm%. The sensitivity is improved by 28% after coating with Ti2C-MXene nanosheet.

articleTitle: Layered Asymmetrically Clipped Optical SCFDM based on Adaptive LDPC Puncturing for IM/DD Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An adaptive LDPC puncturing method suitable for L-ACO-SCFDM is proposed. The simulation results show that it can obtain 6~7dB sensitivity gain compared with conventionalL-ACO-SCFDM and have potential application in short-distance IM/DD optical transmission system.

articleTitle: Simulation of Refractive Index Sensor Based on Microring Resonator
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In the work reported here, we modeled a refractive index sensor based on microrings. This strategy has been applied with success in COMSOL Multiphysics. The proposed structure's free spectral range, sensitivity, and quality factor have received the majority of this study's attention. The resonant cavity refractive index sensor has been shown to function more effectively when the core layer width is close to micron size, the microring width is 1 $\mu \mathrm{m}$, and the radius is 34 $\mu \mathrm{m}$. Its quality factor is 224.67, its free spectral range is 16 nm, and its sensitivity is 160 nm/RIU, correspondingly.

articleTitle: Application of Trellis-Coded Modulation in Long-Haul Optical Fiber Transmissions
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we explore the application of trellis-coded modulation (TCM) in long-haul optical fiber transmissions. We discuss the benefits of TCM in linear transmission as well as degradation in the nonlinear region.

articleTitle: Temperature insensitive pressure sensor based on a novel cascaded all-fiber structure
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We have proposed a fiber-optic gas pressure sensor based on the Mach-Zehnder interference with a novel cascaded all-fiber structure. It has a gas pressure sensitivity of 1 nm/MPa and a very low temperature crosstalk.

articleTitle: Low threshold cascaded Raman random fiber laser with hybrid Erbium-Raman gain
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A low-threshold cascaded Raman random fiber laser is proposed based on the hybrid Erbium-Raman gain in a 90 m-long ultra-high numerical aperture fiber cascaded with a 25 m-long erbium-doped fiber pump with a 1480 nm laser diode. Experimental results show that the threshold pump power is only 67 mW. Under a low pump power of 500 mW, five orders of Raman Stokes are achieved with center wavelengths of 1565, 1681, 1810, 1966 and 2153 nm, respectively. Time domain characteristics measurements indicates that Q-switched laser pulses are produced and it should be the high peak power of these laser pulse that gives rise to the generation of high order Raman stokes components.

articleTitle: Photonic Reservoir Computing Based on Reflective Semiconductor Optical Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a time-delayed photonic reservoir computing structure utilizing a reflective semiconductor optical amplifier. Simulation results indicate that improved time series prediction performance can be achieved, compared to the traditional reservoir computing system.

articleTitle: QAM Signal DSP Algorithm Based on Linear Optical Sampling
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This article proposes a linear optical sampling DSP algorithm scheme for equalization of high-order QAM signals. The EVM of 16QAM and 32QAM signals balanced by the new algorithm have decreased by approximately 14%.

articleTitle: A method to alleviate crosstalk of multiple adjacent carriers in Nyquist DWDM system
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this study, a method to alleviate crosstalk of adjacent carriers in Nyquist system is proposed. This method is verified in 16QAM Nyquist simulation system where the carrier spacing is equal to the baud rate.

articleTitle: Design of multi-carrier probe pulse for coherent fading suppression in Φ-OTDR system
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A multi-carrier pulse is designed to eliminate coherent fading in DAS. A single AOM is used in the system for multi-carrier signal generation, and the fading suppression of $\Phi -$OTDR is achieved by processing the backscattering signals in the subcarriers.

articleTitle: Compact Half Adder on SOI Platform with Inverse Design
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a compact half adder for optical combinational logic circuits. The device shows high transmission and flat spectrum with acceptable phase difference limit and controlled minimum feature size, making it robust for fabrication.

articleTitle: Simulation of the ion beam at the atmospheric pressure interface of a mass spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The selection of a simulation model is a crucial factor in the analysis of ion motion and the design of a mass spectrometer. This is due to the intricate physical field composition of the mass spectrometer and its multi-stage vacuum setup, which necessitates the utilization of simulation techniques. The selection of a suitable simulation model is contingent upon the analyte and the surrounding physical environment. Simulating the gas in the capillary, we solve the Navier-Stokes equation to ascertain the physical state of particles at the exit, incorporating this into the tube-skimmer model. To determine the ultimate ion transport efficiency, we simulate the collision of ions with the background gas instead of the flow field and validate this experiment

articleTitle: High performance C+L-band EDFA enhanced by using a long-period fiber grating
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A simple method to improve gain bandwidth of double-pass C+L-band erbium-doped fiber amplifier (EDFA) is demonstrated by using Bi/Er co-doped fiber (BEDF) and a long-period fiber grating. The achieved 20 dB gain bandwidth is up to 78 nm, covering 1530-1608 nm, with a minimum noise figure of 4.8 dB.

articleTitle: Satellite Optical Signal Modulation Identification Based on Multiple Features and SVM
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To address the signal modulation identification problem in satellite optical communication, a signal identification scheme based on multiple features and support vector machines is proposed, and the feasibility and superiority of this scheme are demonstrated.

articleTitle: NO2 Scheimpflug lidar based on wavelengthswitchable continuous wave external cavity diode laser
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We have developed a high-power laser (3W) with a central wavelength of approximately 450 nm by using a grating external cavity modulation and applied it to the NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> differential lidar system.

articleTitle: Effect of Low Frequency Vibration of Sensing Coil on Fiber Optic Current Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: FOCS current signals are measured by LIA when sensing coils under low frequency vibrations $(\mathbf{1 0} \sim \mathbf{2 0 H z})$. After FFT, it was found that the vibration frequency under $17 \mathrm{~Hz}$ has the greatest influence on the output results.

articleTitle: Blockchain-enabled Data Security Management for Optical Network Telemetry
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a blockchain-enabled security management scheme for telemetry data collection, storage, and access in optical networks. The designed smart contracts are deployed in the Ethereum blockchain, and its functions are tested and verified.

articleTitle: Dynamic Bandwidth allocation algorithm based on traffic classification with the aid of LSTM and GRU for industrial passive optical networks
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: With the rapid development of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), the Industrial Passive Optical Network (IPON) has become an important technology to meet the future needs of access networks due to its deterministic and low latency. However, due to the traffic characteristics of IoT devices, the traditional dynamic bandwidth allocation method cannot make full use of network bandwidth, resulting in low resource utilization. We propose an algorithm to jointly predict classified IoT/non-IoT traffic using LSTM and GRU neural networks, and dynamically allocate bandwidth to SDN-based IPON networks according to the classification results. Results show that it reduces latency by 15.5% and packet losses by 47% under a load of 0.6, compared to existing typical dynamic methods.

articleTitle: Study of femtosecond laser multi-step 3D nanoprinting method
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper utilizes femtosecond laser multiphoton lithography to perform multi-step 3D nanoprinting of different parts of the printing model on glass slide. This method can be used in microstructure integration of polymer devices.

articleTitle: Rogue waves among noise-like pulses
