publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The effects of the saturable absorber and pump power on generating optical rogue waves in a noise-like pulse background are studied. The research results show that cavity parameters regulate the occurrence probability of rogue waves.

articleTitle: Target Transfer of Ferroelectric Thin Films for Electro-Optic Modulation on SOI Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Electro-optical modulators play an essential role in high-capacity fiber optic transmission systems and high-speed optoelectronic information processing systems. In this work, we demonstrate target transfer of ferroelectric thin films for electro-optic modulation on SOI platform. Our BTO hybrid integrated MZI modulator has exhibited a $V_\pi L$ as low as 1.67 $\text{V}\bullet \text{cm}$, and the PTO hybrid integrated micro-ring modulator exhibits an effective electro-optical coefficient $r_{eff}$ as 6 pm/V, which open up new possibilities and approaches for implementing compact electro-optical modulators.

articleTitle: Thin Piezoelectric Sheet Assisted Unobtrusive IMZI-BCG Sensor with PGC-DCM Demodulation
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate an unobtrusive ballistocardiogram (BCG) monitor using an integrated Mach-Zehnder interferometer (IMZI) separately molded with silicone rubber and epoxy resin, where the phase is demodulated with PGC-DCM algorithm assisted with a thin piezoelectric sheet.

articleTitle: Microplastic Sensors Based on Tilted Fiber Bragg Grating and Engineered Peptides
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper presents a microplastic sensor that utilizes a tilted fiber Bragg grating surface plasmon resonance modified with a polystyrene-binding peptide. The sensor design includes an tilted fiber Bragg grating surrounded by a 50 nm thick gold layer. The PSBP, modified with thiol, self-assembles on the gold surface through a Au-S bond. This peptide biosensor is capable of specifically binding to polystyrene microplastics through hydrophobic. It can effectively detect PS microplastics in water within the concentration range of 1 mg/ml to 1 $\mu$g/ml.

articleTitle: Research on Evaluation Method of Ship EMC Based on Multi-layer Coupling Network
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes the method based on multi-layer coupled networks to evaluate ship electromagnetic compatibility (EMC). Firstly, based on the theory of multi-layer coupled network systems, the equipment and their transmission link that mainly influence the ship EMC are defined as the nodes and edges of the evaluation model; Secondly, the network layers of the different domain of the evaluation model are located, as well as the coupling methods between the layers are provided; Then, according to the characteristics of the multi-layer network model, the evaluation method of the influence of the key nodes on the ship’s EMC is given; Finally, the effectiveness of the evaluation method of ship EMC based on multi-layer coupled network is verified by analyzing several frequency using equipment on the ship. This method has certain reference significance and development prospects in the field of the evaluation of ship EMC.

articleTitle: Transceiver imperfections compensation and calibration methods
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We review the relevant progress and advances of modeling, measurement and compensation of the linear and nonlinear imperfections in optical coherent transceivers, and we also discuss some open issues that still need to be addressed.

articleTitle: A Superimposed Fiber Grating Sensor for Simultaneous Measurement Bending and Temperature
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel superimposed fiber grating sensor for bending and temperature measurement has been proposed. The sensor exhibited high bending and temperature sensitivities of $17.096 \mathrm{~nm} / \mathrm{m}^{-1}$ and $-0.238 \mathrm{~nm} /^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, respectively.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Methods for the Pseudo Mode Problem in OAM Fiber FEM simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper uses different machine learning models and thus validates the potential of machine learning to solve the pseudo mode problem during OAM fiber simulation.

articleTitle: A Technical Review of Integrated Sensing and Communication in Optical Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We investigate the state of art technologies of integrated sensing and communication in optical transmission system. A detailed comparison is conducted among the available solutions. Meanwhile, the potential research directions and challenges are also discussed.

articleTitle: 3×3 Microfiber Coupler Simulation and RI Sensing Performance with Output end Sagnac Loop
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An optical fiber 3×3 microfiber coupler (MFC) is fabricated by fusing taper method. The working principle of the MFC is theoretically analyzed, the optical field of the MFC with different coupling degrees is theoretically simulated. The liquid refractive index (RI) sensing performance of the MFC with output Sagnac loop is experimentally studied, and its highest sensitivity is 25108nm/RIU. Theoretical and experimental results show that the wavelength has tunable characteristics, which can be used in tunable filters and wavelength division multiplexers, and the sensing characteristics have potential applications in biomedical diagnosis, environmental monitoring, food safety monitoring, and other fields.

articleTitle: Reliability-Aware DQN-based Optimization Method of Initial Mapping Solutions in Optical Network-on- Chip (ONoC)
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Optical Network-on-Chip (ONoC) provides a promising solution for on-chip communication with higher bandwidth and lower latency, compared to traditional Electrical Network-on-Chip (ENoC). However, the reliability challenges (such as insertion loss and crosstalk) exist in ONoC. As for this issue, reliability-aware mapping can be considered. This work proposes a reliability-aware DQN-based optimization method of initial mapping solutions in ONoC, to generate better initial mapping solutions. This optimization method of initial mapping solutions can be combined with existing mapping algorithms, further improving the mapping performance. The evaluation results show that for a given core graph and network topology, our proposed method generates better solutions compared to the traditional random method. Also, the proposed method is helpful for finding the optimal mapping solution more efficiently when combined with the existing mapping algorithms.

articleTitle: Hardware-Based Algorithm Acceleration towards Efficient Network Traffic Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Network traffic utilization finds extensive applications in network management, network security, IT business, and various other fields. The traffic utilization process comprises three stages: traffic collection, traffic storage, and traffic analysis application. The network traffic storage system serves as the fundamental foundation for traffic utilization. However, the rapid growth in network performance and the diversification of network applications pose significant challenges to the design of network traffic storage systems, including concerns over traffic storage overhead and traffic processing overhead. In this paper, we introduce an efficient network traffic storage system design, which applies three algorithms—compression, decompression, and sorting—to achieve storage efficiency and traffic query efficiency. Furthermore, we explore the utilization of efficient hardware to accelerate these key algorithms. Additionally, we provide a preliminary evaluation of the effect of hardware acceleration.

articleTitle: Blocking-Driven Spectrum Defragmentation Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning in Tidal Elastic Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a tidal-aware spectrum defragmentation using deep reinforcement learning in elastic optical networks with tidal traffic, which balances reconfiguration times and blocking performance. Simulation results verify the 7% reduction of blocking rate.

articleTitle: Selenisation optimization for nanoparticle based CIGSSe solar cells
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Good selenization conditions are key to the performance enhancement of copper indium gallium sulfur selenide (CIGSSe) solar cells based on copper indium gallium sulphide ($\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{In}, \mathrm{Ga}) \mathrm{S}_{2}$) nanoparticle ink. Suitable selenization conditions are able to promote the growth of large grains in the light-absorbing layer of CIGSSe thin films, thus improving the CIGSSe solar cells performance and are of great importance for their industrialization. In this paper, $\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{In}, \mathrm{Ga}) \mathrm{S}_{2}$ nanoparticle were synthesized and their precursor thin filmw were selenised into a light-absorbing layers with large grains. After the selenization conditions were optimized, the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of the CIGSSe devices was $10.84 \%$. Using Xray diffraction (XRD) and field emission scanning electron microscopy (SEM) characterization methods, we found that under the optimized selenization conditions, sufficient large grain crystals produced in light absorbing layers which helps increase the device efficiency.

articleTitle: High-precision mode purity measurement of few-mode ring core fibers
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Mode purity measurement is crucial for various applications utilizing few-mode fibers and related devices. We propose a simple and accurate method for measuring the mode purity of the output optical field in few-mode ring-core fiber (RCF). Mode purity can be calculated solely from the outgoing intensity distribution with high precision. We demonstrate our approach experimentally and verify it by off-axis digital holography technology in a few-mode RCF supporting four mode groups at 1550 nm.

articleTitle: Fast Power Tilt Estimation for Dynamic C+L-Band Links after Fiber Cut
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper finds that C-band channels plays a more important role in fiber cut scenarios and derives a simple metric for estimation of power tilt after sudden fiber cut in C+L-band transmission systems.

articleTitle: Beam intensity shaping with a 3D printed on-fiber microlens
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Spatial beam intensity shaping is important in various applications, including laser fabrication and medical treatment. In this study we present a new method for doughnut beam shaping using a 3D nanoprinted on-fiber microlens. The optical structure of the microlens was initially designed and optimized using software based on illumination optics. Subsequently, the microlens was fabricated onto the tip of a single-mode fiber employing the technique of femtosecond laser-induced two-photon polymerization. By using the fiber-tip microlens, both simulation and experimental results have demonstrated the successful transformation of the Gaussian beam emitted from a single-mode fiber into a high-quality doughnut beam. The proposed microlens shows larger tolerance in fabrication resolution compared with optical diffraction beam shaping elements.

articleTitle: Spatial-Temporal Prediction Model for Optical Fronthaul Network Traffic based on ASTFN
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes a traffic prediction model for optical fronthaul network called attention-based spatial-temporal fusion neural network (ASTFN), combining convolutional neural network (CNN) capturing the spatial dependencies between fronthaul traffic, and long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network obtaining temporal feature. Fusion strategy is adopted to reduce the phenomenon of information loss due to preference expression in CNN by concatenate the original traffic matrix and spatial feature extraction result. Self-attention mechanism in LSTM captures the noteworthy information in sliding window, improving the expressing capability of temporal dependency. The experimental results show that the model proposed in this paper has better prediction results and higher prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Prediction Time-Based Spectrum RMSA Algorithm for Hybrid AR and IR Services in EONs
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose an algorithm for scheduling and distance adaption of hybrid AR and IR services based on time prediction. Simulation results show that the algorithm can effectively reduce the service blocking probability.

articleTitle: Absorber Layer Etching Optimization for Nanoparticle Ink Based CuInGa (S,Se)2 Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The optimization of etching conditions for the absorber layer of high-performance copper indium gallium selenide solar cells based on nanoparticle ink is of great significance to improve device efficiency by forming OVC at surface and large grain. Using bromine-methanol solution to etch the absorber layer is more environmentally friendly than using the highly toxic potassium cyanide. In this paper, by adjusting the concentration of the bromine-methanol etching solution and the etching time, the best power conversion efficiency of the CIGSSe device reached 10.42%.

articleTitle: On-line Monitoring Method for Burial Depth of Submarine Cable Based on Distributed Optical Fiber Acoustic Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: By analyzing the external marine ambient noise field captured by the existed dark fiber inside the submarine cable, a new buried depth monitoring method of submarine cable based on distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) is proposed.

articleTitle: Optimization of Na+ Doping in Absorb Layer for Nanoparticles Based on Cu(In,Ga)Se2 Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The CIGS nanoparticle route in solution processes is of great importance for large-scale fabrication of thin-film solar cells. Alkali metal such as Na doping can passivate grain boundaries, increase carrier concentration, reduce point defects and promote CIGS crystal growth<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>. In this paper, CIGS thin films which were spin-coated with nanoparticle inks were doped with Na<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> after annealing, before the selenization process to form CIGSSe crystal absorber layers. By optimizing the Na<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> concentration in the solution and immersion time, the best power conversion efficiency obtained as 10.13%. The crystal surface and cross-section of the absorber layer were investigated using field emission scanning electron microscopy and EDS characterization, which confirmed that the successful doping of Na<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> facilitated the crystal growth.

articleTitle: Study on the Mechanism of Coarse Mode Selection in Parity-Time-Symmetric Optoelectronic Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The influence of coarse mode selection in parity-time (PT) symmetric optoelectronic oscillator (OEO) on side-mode suppression ratio (SMSR) is studied. A single-mode oscillation at 9.98GHz with an SMSR of 56dB is experimentally realized.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison Between Core and Cladding Pump Schemes for Weakly-coupled Multi-core EDFAs
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Performance between core and cladding pump schemes are simulatively compared based on weakly-coupled 7-core-single-mode and 7-core-3-mode EDFs. The results show that the two schemes have significant performance difference in noise figure and power conversion efficiency.

articleTitle: A Relative Humidity Sensor with a Fiber Tip All-Polymer Microcavity
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A fast response relative humidity (RH) sensor with a fiber tip pentaerythritol tetraacrylate (PETA) based all-polymer microcavity is presented. The fiber tip all-polymer microcavity, with a maximum size of $99.27 \mu \mathrm{m}$, consists of a circular truncated cone on the fiber tip end surface and is manufactured by photopolymerization of PETA using two-photon polymerization technology, which is characterized by miniaturization and rapid manufacturing. It is a promising candidate for potential applications in chemical, medical and biological fields related to RH detection.

articleTitle: Non-invasive Blood Pressure Monitoring Based on Smart Mattress Embeded with Fiber MZI-BCG Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a photoplethysmography (PPG) enabled non-invasive blood pressure monitoring system using a smart mattress, where a compact high sensitive Mach-Zehdner interferometer (MZI) is embedded.

articleTitle: Modulation format identification based on horizontal projection and LSTM in optical networks
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes a horizontal projection (HP) and long short-term memory neural network (LSTM) scheme for modulation format identification (MFI). The results show the proposed scheme achieves 100% MFI accuracy for the five modulation formats.

articleTitle: The Multiplexing Mode for OFDM Passive Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: we briefly overview the advanced multiplexing scheme and the according key digital signal processing in optical access network based on orthogonal frequency division multiplexing passive optical network transmission in the enhanced next-generation optical access networks.

articleTitle: D-shaped terahertz microstructured fiber biosensor based on plasmon resonance on graphene surface
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper designs a D-shaped microstructured fiber optic biosensing model based on surface plasmon resonance of graphene, which is dedicated to the terahertz frequency band. Improving optical fiber sensing performance by adjusting graphene thickness and graphene chemical potential to increase peak spectral loss. The optimization results show that the resonance peak decreases with increasing excitation layer thickness and graphene chemical potential. Moreover, the higher the graphene chemical potential, the more the resonance spectrum is shifted towards the higher frequency band. The maximum frequency sensitivity is 1300 GHz/RIU over a refractive index sensing range of 1.1-1.5, corresponding to a quality factor of $1.0\times 10^{4}$ RIU. In conclusion, the proposed D-type microstructured optical fiber has a novel and ingenious structure with high detection accuracy. With graphene as the excitation medium, the microstructured optical fiber operating band is successfully extended to the terahertz band, opening up a broader application prospect for the microstructured optical fiber structure in the THz sensing field.
