articleTitle: Extended Kalman Filter Scheme for Modal Dispersion Compensation in Mode Division Multiplexing Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose an extended Kalman-filter scheme for modal-dispersion compensation in MDM systems and implement compensation of a large differential group delay of 170 ps. The results verify the effectiveness of our scheme in MDM systems.

articleTitle: Microring Modulators Based Optical Matrix-matrix Multiplication Accelerators
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and simulate a highly parallel, scalable and compact optical neural network accelerator which is able to perform matrix-matrix multiplication based on the microring modulators. Simulation results confirm its feasibility for matrix-matrix multiplication.

articleTitle: Generation of the high-frequency tunable linear frequency modulation signal based on optical fiber frequency shift loop
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Optical Linear frequency modulation (LFM) waveform generation based on optical frequency shift loop (OFSL) is theoretically analyzed and demonstrated by simulation. By Heterodyne beating with frequency-tunable local oscillator in balanced photo local oscillator in balanced photo-detector, a high frequency, tunable LFM signal can be generated.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Hierarchical SDN Orchestration for End-to-End Key Provisioning in Large-Scale Quantum Key Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate end-to-end key provisioning among multiple QKDNs with a hierarchical SDN orchestration architecture, where the computational complexity is reduced via abstracted hierarchical network views and the seconds-level latency without manual intervention is achieved.

articleTitle: Deep learning-based SPGD algorithm for hybrid vector modes decomposition and reconstruction in spatial light paths
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A deep learning-based stochastic parallel gradient descent algorithm is proposed to accurately obtain the modal coefficients of cylindrical vectors in spatial optical paths. The decomposition and reconstruction of mixed vector modes are experimentally realized.

articleTitle: An Optical Fiber Thermal Anemometer with Full Light Reflection
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An optical fiber thermal anemometer using laser-heated Fabry-Perot interferometer(FPI) is proposed. FPI is manufactured at the tip of germanium-doped fiber using a UV-curing adhesive. The pump light source is the heating light source, and the broadband light source is the detection light source. The interference spectrum of FPI changes with the change of wind speed, and the change of FPI cavity length is not only thermal expansion and contraction caused by temperature, but also strain caused by wind, so we determine the specific value of wind speed by detecting the drift of the interference spectrum. Through experiments, the sensitivity of the low-speed region can reach - 4.27nm/(m ● s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">- 1</sup>), and the sensitivity of the high-speed region in the measurement range of 0-8m/s is also stable at -0.14nm/(m ● s-1).

articleTitle: Thermal Blooming Induced Mode Crosstalk of Bessel-Gaussian Beams Propagating in the Atmosphere
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Bessel-Gaussian (BG) beams have the potential to be utilized in laser atmospheric engineering applications, such as directed energy and space optical communication. The study investigates the impact of thermal blooming on single Bessel-Gaussian (sBG) and multiple Bessel-Gaussian (mBG) beams propagating in the atmosphere, employing the multi-phase screen method and the fast Fourier transform to solve the thermal blooming equation. Due to the intensity and phase distortion caused by thermal blooming, phenomena such as phase singularity splitting, orbital angular momentum spectrum spreading, and mode crosstalk appear. The mode crosstalk of sBG beams can be mitigated by reducing the radial wave number. In contrast, the relative crosstalk energy of mBG beams decreases with the difference value of initial angular quantum number. Consequently, beams with a larger initial angular quantum number difference exhibit weaker mode crosstalk due to thermal blooming.

articleTitle: Numerical and Experimental Investigation of Quasi - Coherent Soliton Pulses in a Fiber Laser
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We numerically investigate quasi-coherent soliton pulses formation in a fiber laser. Conventional solitons experience transitional breathing and collapsing regions, and gradually evolve into quasi-coherent soliton pulses. The simulation is consistent with experimental results.

articleTitle: Modeling Analysis of the Temperature Transfer of OPGW Under Ice Coating
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, the temperature transfer of optical fiber composite overhead ground wire under ice coating is analyzed by finite-element method. The simulation results provide a basis for the theoretical study of fiber optic cable icing.

articleTitle: Label-Free DNA Biosensing Based on Fiber Sensors Functionalized by 3D Nanostructure Probes
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Label-free DNA biosensors using fiber sensors achieve ultra-low limit DNA biosensing, sensing interfaces of microcavity, fiber bragg grating as well as photonic crystal fiber are functionalized by DNA 3D nanostructure probes with size of nm.

articleTitle: Gain Optimization in Erbium-Ytterbium Co-Doped Hybrid Slot Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An on-chip optical amplifier based on an erbium-ytterbium co-doped hybrid slot waveguide is designed. The modal characteristics are optimized by combining the slot overlap factors and the effective modal area to improve its gain performance.

articleTitle: On-board Hybrid Heterogeneous Distributed Computing Resource Virtualization
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: It is necessary to develop a real-time fault-tolerant high-performance computing architecture to enhance the efficiency and performance of on-board applications, the architecture would provide a shared, unified, and scalable computing platform utilizing various hybrid heterogeneous resources such as CPU, DSP, FPGA, and GPU. In this paper, we propose an abstract method for modeling the energy consumption of heterogeneous computing resources and establish performance models for each resource. By enabling dynamic allocation and elastic expansion of on-board hybrid heterogeneous distributed computers based on user needs, we aim to achieve maximum computing energy efficiency and service quality.

articleTitle: High-sensitivity FBG-FP Interference Coarse and Precise Temperature Measurement Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This study introduces a temperature sensing mechanism of heightened sensitivity through the evaluation of fringe visibility and the Vernier effect within an FBG-FP (Fiber Bragg Grating - Fabry-Perot) setup. By amalgamating two cleaved single-mode fibers (SMFs) within a capillary tube, an FP microcavity is crafted. Notably, one extremity of the SMF is affixed with a silver coating to bolster reflectivity. The infusion of liquid crystal (LC) materials into the FP cavity introduces birefringence, thus catalyzing the emergence of a Vernier phenomenon. Consequently, any alterations in temperature result in proportional shifts in the LC’s effective refractive index. The temperature sensitivity herein is deduced by monitoring peak shifts within the periodic Vernier envelope. The experiment shows that adding FBG technology can achieve coarse range temperature measurement, and the sensitivity of FP can reach 42.35 nm/°C. FBG can improve the coarse accuracy measurement of sensors, with a sensitivity of 9.98 pm/°C. The inherent simplicity of the sensor construction and demodulation process highlights the advantages of this method.

articleTitle: High Repetition Rate Linear Sweep Frequency DFB Laser Based on A Photoelectric Feedback Loop
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A high-repetition-rate linear scanning scheme based on a photoelectric feedback loop and consisting of an self-heterodyne optical link and a phase-locked electrical link is proposed. By using a pre-modulated current waveform, the nonlinear error of the linear sweep triangular output can be reduced, and the error can be captured by the phase-locked loop. Then, a phase-locked feedback loop is implemented to reduce the nonlinear error of the laser output. This scheme utilizes a simple commercial DFB laser as the light source. The system can achieve optimized linearity of the 31.25 kHz repetition rate triangular sweep. The maximum error can be optimized from 6% to 0.5%. The linear regression constant of triangular sweep is optimized from $1.7 \times 10^{-3}$ to $1 \times 10^{-5}$. In addition, the extraction and processing methods of error signals were theoretically analyzed.

articleTitle: A method for detecting the accuracy of optical measurement module
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In order to test the accuracy of an optical measurement module, from the per-spective of practicability, this paper uses photoelectric theodolite and mirror to build an autocollimation optical path, and designs a method to test the accuracy of optical measurement module. According to the readings of photoelectric the-odolite and optical measurement module, the measurement range and error of optical measurement module are quickly detected, and the accuracy of optical measurement module is conveniently detected.

articleTitle: Full Bandwidth Wavelength Division Multiplexer Based on Silicon-on-insulator Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we design a self-imaging multimode interference (MMI) device with oblique incidence waveguides based on silicon-on-insulator (SOI) platform. It can work as a 4-channel full-band wavelength division multiplex (WDM) device.

articleTitle: The Research on a Tunable Self-oscillating Multicarrier Light Source
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A tunable self-oscillating multicarrier source based on recirculating frequency shift loop and optoelectronic oscillator is proposed. 60 subcarriers with 2.48 dB flatness and tunable frequency intervals from 3.1 GHz to 16.5 GHz are experimentally achieved.

articleTitle: Research on the Two-stage Kalman Filtering Algorithm for Joint Compensation of Phase and Amplitude Noise
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper utilizes a two-stage Kalman filter to compensate for phase and amplitude noise in a 64QAM optical transmission system. The results show an OSNR improvement of 0.1-0.6 dB over BPS and LKF.

articleTitle: Extraction of group refractive index of silicon waveguide using two racetrack resonators
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We present the extraction of group refractive index of a silicon waveguide of $450 \mathrm{~nm} \times 220 \mathrm{~nm}$ with a slab of 70 nm using the spectral responses of two racetrack resonators with perimeters of $405.66 \mu \mathrm{m}$ and $505.66 \mu \mathrm{m}$, respectively. We assume a cubic polynomial relation between the effective refractive index and the wavelength. An analytic expression for the group refractive indexes of both straight and bend waveguides can be obtained using the two measured spectra. The calculated $n_{\mathrm{g}}$ at 1550 nm is 3.922. This method offers a simple calibration tool in the optical delay line design.

articleTitle: Capillary-Based Structural Long-Period Gratings for High-Sensitivity Curvature and Strain Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A structural long-period gratings built with cascaded-sections of capillaries for high-sensitive curvature and strain measurement is proposed and experimentally demonstrated, and the correspondent sensitivities of 29.58 dB/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and -18.9 pm/$\mu \varepsilon$ could be achieved, respectively.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional CAP Modulation Optical Transmission System Based on McEliece Encryption
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A three-dimensional carrier-less amplitude phase (CAP) modulation scheme based on McEliece encryption is proposed and verified by experiment. Through post-quantum encryption, higher dimensional and more secure optical transmission is realized.

articleTitle: High-performance SERS Substrates via the Plasmonic Micro-nano Structure and MOF-Enabled Molecular Preconcentration Effect
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Two kinds of SERS substrates are proposed. Where, the hot-spots are achieved with plasmonic nanogap, and the number of hot-spots significantly increased through 3D structure. Furthermore, MOFs’ preconcentration effect can enrich analytes in the hot-spots.

articleTitle: Highly sensitive carbon dioxide sensor based on guanidine derivative polymer functionalized Fabry-Perot interferometer
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A highly sensitive carbon dioxide (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) sensor based on a fiber Fabry-Perot interferometer (FPI) is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The sensor is fabricated by splicing a hollow core capillary (HCC) at the end of a single mode fiber (SMF), coated by a CO <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas-sensitive film polyhexamethylene biguanide (PHMB). The FPI cavity is formed between the splicing point and the PHMB film, and the reflected light of the two surfaces interferes resulting in an interference peak in the reflection spectrum.

articleTitle: Low-Loss All-Fiber Mode Multiplexers for Weakly-Coupled 4-Mode Fiber
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we report an all-fiber 4-mode fiber multiplexer and its measurement, which uses a fused tapering method to fabricate different mode-selective coupler. The insertion loss of a single mode-selective is less than 0.7dB, the insertion loss of LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf>, LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>, LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> and LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> is less than 3 dB after cascading, while the modal crosstalk is lower than −15dB. This device can be applied in mode-division multiplexing transmission systems.

articleTitle: Scalable ultra-low loss 5-LP mode selective coupler
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The 5-LP mode selection coupler (MSC) with ultra-low loss is designed and manufactured, with losses as low as 0.1 dB, providing excellent cascading performance to achieve low-cost high-performance space division multiplexing.

articleTitle: Research on the Delayed Diagonal Zipper Codes Based on Periodic Truncation
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A modified zipper code scheme is proposed, which employs the periodic truncation and time delay to avoid error propagation. The simulation results show that input BER threshold raised by 1.2E-4 and 1E-3 respectively by increasing mapping delay and reducing truncated length.

articleTitle: Research on Sensing of Orbital Changes of Spatial Target Based on Space-based Optical Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper establishes the sensing model of space target movement in space-based optical detection based on Kalman filter, and simulates and analyzes the results of target movement sensing time in different orbit change situations.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of PS-1024-QAM Transmission over 22.5-km MCF with Pre-Compensation
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The Volterra pre-compensation algorithm based on dynamic deviation reduction is proposed in this paper, and experimentally demonstrated its performance in the polarization multiplexed PS-1024-QAM transmission with capacity of 348.5-Gbit/s.

articleTitle: Hot-wire anemometer using cobalt-doped fiber based grating Fabry-Perot interferometer
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An optically-heated hot-wire anemometer using a cobalt-doped fiber based grating Fabry-Perot interferometer (FPI) is proposed. The 800 $\mu \mathrm{m}$-long cobalt-doped fiber sandwiched between two fiber Bragg gratings absorbs the heating laser and increases the cavity length of the FPI due to temperature increase. Its temperature drops with airflow velocity that shifts the fringe wavelength of the FPI. Experimental results show a measurement range of 0-4 m/s with a sensitivity of -867 pm/(m/s) at airflow velocity of 0.1 m/s.

articleTitle: Energy-efficient variable optical attenuator on SOI with folded waveguides and heaters
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report a variable optical attenuator (VOA) on silicon-on-insulator (SOI) with folded silicon waveguides and TiW heaters to improve the thermal efficiency. The measured extinction ratio of the device is around 20.4 dB with a power consumption of 10.2 mW. The rise and fall times are 17.2 μs and 17.55 μs, respectively.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Self-Absorption Correction Method for Fan-Beam X-ray Fluorescence CT
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: During fan-beam X-ray fluorescence computational tomography imaging, the attenuation of incident X-ray and fluorescence x-ray cause poor reconstructed image quality. In this study, a U-net based method is proposed for self-absorption correction in X-ray fluorescence CT. The numerical simulation results show that the well-trained neural network can recover internal structure in sinogram domain and improves image quality by reconstructing complete projection data.

articleTitle: simultaneous illumination-imaging system
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Micromulti-quantum well (MQW) III-nitride diodes are commonly used as microleds and are considered the next generation of display and imaging technology. Among other things, they theoretically have the ability to detect and modulate light. Here, we integrate MQWs Type III-nitride diode monolithic onto a chip to establish a real-time imaging system for image reconstruction, which can perform simultaneous illumination imaging operations in practice. These functions can be controlled by software. This device, if integrated on a large scale, could lead to multifunctional displays that combine millions of III-nitride diodes to perform these functions simultaneously for simultaneous illumination-imaging.

articleTitle: Fast Routing Algorithm Based on Topology Pruning in Mega Satellite Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Satellite laser communication is gaining more and more attention, leading to rapid expansion of the scale of optical satellite networks. However, when the network scales up significantly, routing calculation time will become unmanageable, due to the increased time complexity of the routing algorithm resulting from the growing number of nodes and links. To address this issue, a topology-pruning based fast routing (TPFR) scheme for mega satellite optical networks is proposed in this paper. By establishing a representation of satellite optical networks and implementing topology pruning using regression tree method, the routing process is completed with reduced calculation time in small sub-graph. Simulation results show that TPFR can reduce routing calculation time by more than 45% compared to traditional routing algorithms.

articleTitle: Laser Wavelength Measurement using a Fabry-Perot Interferometer
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Wavelength measurement is required in many laser applications, in this paper, we built a precise Fabry-Perot interferometer for near infrared cavity ring-down spectroscopy. The interferometer is formed by a 2mm thick etalon of Schott Zerodur glass, providing a free spectral range of about 50GHz, and two InGaAs amplified photodetectors with maximum bandwidths up to 5MHz. The experimental results showed a good linearity in narrow frequency windows of 18.5GHz, which nearly covers the entire gas absorption linewidth. By using the ratio of the reflected signal to the transmitted signal of the etalon, the fine wavelength could be determined from a DFB laser with a 3σ detection limit of 27MHz. And the interferometer accuracy was measured about 125MHz compared with a commercial wavelength meter. Besides it has fast response, simple structure, and can be used to deduce the exact quantity of the trace gases.

articleTitle: Spatial Pilot-aided Fast-adapt Framework for Image Transmission through Long Multi-mode Fibers
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a pilot-aided learning framework for stable and accurate image transmission through multi-mode fiber. A fast-adapt strategy is developed to allow online model tuning with 1% pilot frames for $\gt50\min$ transmission in 100m fiber.

articleTitle: Secure VLC System with Joint IRS Design and Cooperative Jamming
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A joint intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) design and cooperative Jamming strategy is proposed to improve the physical layer security (PLS) for multiple-input single-output (MISO) VLC systems with eavesdroppers. Specifically, IRS is used to enhance the legitimate users’ reception while the cooperative Jamming signals disturb the eavesdropper’s reception to the greatest extent without affecting the legitimate users. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme significantly increases users’ signal to interference plus noise ratio (SINR) and reduces eavesdroppers’ SINR, thereby enhancing the secrecy sum-rate and improving the security of the system.

articleTitle: Calibration of Elasticity Coefficient for Dual-Ring Optical Pressure Measurement Device
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Microcantilever device is used for laser power measurement by the optical pressure method, combined with an interferometer to convert the power signal to a displacement signal for measurement. We designed a dual-ring microcantilever device and calibrated the elasticity coefficient of the device using standard weights and an interferometer measurement system. The calibration shows that the displacement of the microcantilever device has good linearity, and the measured elastic coefficients are in general agreement with the stress simulation results. By adding a thin glass plate to the surface of the microcantilever device to form a squeeze film air damping, the damped vibration time of the cantilever is greatly shortened and the signal-to-noise ratio is improved, which provides a new feasible idea for fast and accurate measurement of laser power.

articleTitle: On-demand provisioning of computing resources in computing power network with mixed CPU and GPU
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose an on-demand computing provisioning method in computing power network with mixed CPU and GPU. Simulation results validate that more computing tasks can be accommodated by optimizing the usage of heterogeneous computing resources.

articleTitle: CNN Nonlinear Equalizer with Reducing the Dimensionality of Feature Maps
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method of feature map dimensionality reduction as the input of CNN. We validate the complexity advantages of this scheme in a 120Gb/s PDM 64QAM coherent optical communication system.

articleTitle: Research on the performance of 3D-CAP-256QAM signal with superposition
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a novel 3D-CAP-256QAM scheme which composes of constellation overlay is proposed. The results show that the proposed circle-shaped constellation structure shows better BER performance compared with the other two constellation structures.

articleTitle: High Fidelity Wristband Pulse Sensor Based on Fiber MZI Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a wearable fiber pulse sensor based on Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI), which is simply embedded into a commercial wristband such that it can be used to monitor wrist’s weak acoustic signal.

articleTitle: Design of hollow-core negative curvature fiber for the temperature sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this work, a hollow-core negative curvature fiber filled with the ethanol and gold wires is proposed for the temperature sensing. It is demonstrated that the average sensitivity of 3 nm/°C can be achieved in the temperature range of −40 ~ 60°C.

articleTitle: 50 Gb/s faster-than-Nyquist Coherent PON with optimized ISI cancellation scheme
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a faster-than-Nyquist coherent passive optical networks (PON) for 50Gbit/s 100km fiber transmission. The simulation results show the FTN with advanced equalization scheme leads to better performance than conventional PON.

articleTitle: “invisible” pulsation dynamics of soliton molecules in a bidirectional fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel optical soliton dynamics phenomenon, called “invisible” pulsation, has gradually attracted extensive interest in recent years, which can only be identified effectively with the help of real-time spectroscopy technique, i.e., dispersive Fourier transformation (DFT). In this work, based on a new bidirectional passively mode-locked fiber laser (MLFL), the “invisible” pulsation dynamics of soliton molecules (SMs) is systematically studied.

articleTitle: Polarization-Insensitive 1×2 Power Divider on SOI
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report the design of two polarization-insensitive $1 \times 2$ power dividers on SOI with 220nm top silicon. The multimode interference coupler is within 4 $\mu \mathrm{m} \times 140 \mu \mathrm{m}$. For the type I device, the excess losses for both the TE and TM modes at 1550 nm are $\lt 0.1$ dB. For the type II device, the excess losses for the TE and TM modes are $\lt 0.55$ dB over the C band. We also analyze their performance deteriorations due to ±20 nm fabrication errors in width.

articleTitle: Research on Feature Point Recognition of Laser Welding Seam Based on Machine Vision
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper designs and implements a machine vision recognition algorithm system for feature points on the surface of oil pipeline welds. The system consists of a feature point recognition algorithm on the surface of the weld and an abnormal detection processing algorithm. By automatically receiving and processing the weld surface data from the structured light sensor, it can automatically calculate and extract the welds of various shapes of grooves in real time under different working conditions. The seam shape and related parameter data are transmitted to the upper control device in real time through the data communication protocol to realize the automatic control of the welding torch swing, and have certain abnormal processing and anti-interference capabilities. In the actual welding operation on site, the system can accurately and real-time collect data related to the surface morphology of the weld, which lays a solid foundation for the realization of automatic pipeline welding.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Microstrip Dual Band MIMO Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: As an important component of the RF front-end of wireless communication systems, antenna performance has a decisive impact on the communication ability of the system. This paper designs a high isolation microstrip dual frequency multi input multi output (MIMO) antenna. The antenna selects a bent monopole antenna as the front high-frequency resonance unit. By adding a rear resonance unit to introduce low-frequency resonance, it achieves dual frequency operation at 2.4 GHz and 5.2 GHz. The method of slotting on the floor and hanging metal wires on the back solves the mutual coupling problem between antenna elements. The results show that the antenna can achieve dual frequency operation with good isolation, and its gain, out-of-roundness, and other parameters meet the design requirements, meeting the requirements of wireless communication systems for high communication rate and high communication capacity.

articleTitle: A flexible hydraulic optical Fiber senor Based on Fabry-Perot Interferometer for Pulse Pressure Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A flexible hydraulic optical fiber sensor based on Fabry-Perot interferometers(FPI) for pulse wave measurements is proposed. The sensor is fabricated by a single-mode fiber and a gold film forming the FP cavity, with a glycerol-filled liquid capsule structure encapsulated on the outside and sealed with a Polydimethylsiloxane(PDMS) diaphragm. The structure can reduce the pressure measurement error caused by the position offset, realize the accurate detection of the weak pulse wave signal. The proposed alignment-free device has good application prospects for cardiovascular disease prevention and diagnosis.

articleTitle: The Design of Photoacoustic Cell with Multiple Resonances
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We have designed a photoacoustic cell with four resonant cavities with the same radius and different lengths, which can achieve two gas differential detection. The crosstalk existed in the cell are analyzed as well.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of Self-homodyne Coherent Transmission of TPS-4096-QAM over a 22.5 km MCF with a Spectral Efficiency of 19.15 bits/s/Hz/core
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate the self-homodyne coherent transmission of truncated probabilistic shaping (TPS) 4096-level quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) over a 22.5 km 7-core fiber, without carrier recovery. The spectral efficiency can be up to 19.15 bits/s/Hz/core.

articleTitle: A Fast Routing Algorithm with Maximum Throughput in Dynamic LEO Optical Satellite Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel routing algorithm is proposed to reduce the routing computation time in dynamic LEO optical satellite networks. Simulations prove that our proposed algorithm can significantly fasten the computation while maintaining the maximum throughput.

articleTitle: Switchable multi-wavelength thulium-doped fiber random laser by using two-segment Sagnac loop filter
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A switchable multi-wavelength thulium-doped fiber random laser (TDFRL) using a random fiber grating to provide random distributed feedback and a two-segment Sagnac loop filter is proposed. By adjusting two polarization controllers, we achieved switchable laser output with single to five peaks.

articleTitle: An End-to-End Autoencoder For FSO System Under Unknown CSI Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In free-space optical (FSO) communication systems, the maximum likelihood (ML) method is considered as the optimal detector when perfect channel state information (CSI) is available at the receiver. However, in scenarios where CSI is unknown, ML fails to provide satisfactory bit error rate (BER) performance. To address this issue, we propose an end-to-end (E2E) learning method for FSO communication based on convolutional autoencoder (CNN-AE). The proposed method is compared with a conventional FSO system using ML estimation in scenarios with perfect and unknown CSI, as well as varying levels of channel turbulence. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the conventional ML method when CSI is unknown, while achieving equivalent performance to the ML detector under perfect CSI.

articleTitle: All-optical Controllable Micro-ring Filter with a Carbon Nanotube/Polymer/SiO₂ Hybrid Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A short carbon nanotubes (CNTs) nano-film based polymer/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> hybrid waveguide on-chip micro-ring filter is presented. The film can effectively improve the coherent depth and quality factor of the on-chip filter. The filter shows good all-optical controllable performance due to the excellent thermo-optic effect of the CNTs nano-film. Since the chip shows the advantages of small size, compact structure, and all-optical control, and it is expected to have practical applications in optical filters, optical sensors, spectral analysis, and so on.

articleTitle: Adaptive Beam Control for Optical Inter-Satellite Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We present our recent research on adaptive beam control technique for intersatellite laser links. Adverse effects of pointing errors and angular-of-arrival fluctuations are mitigated by adjusting beam divergence and convergence angles adaptively to transmission conditions.

articleTitle: Congestion-aware Adaptive Arbitration for Multipath Routing in Optical Network-on-chip
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an arbitrator-based multipath routing algorithm for optical network-on-chip. Simulation results verify the performance of the algorithm by analyzing end to end delay, optical power consumption, optical loss, and memory usage.

articleTitle: Noise Suppression of All-optical OOK Matching System Based on Cascaded Highly Nonlinear Fiber
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Noise can reduce the performance of the OOK matching system, leading to matching errors. For correct the errors, this paper applies a cascaded noise suppression structure and places it in the recirculating loop of the OOK matching system. The devices of the noise suppression structure used are mainly highly nonlinear fiber (HNLF), all-optical filter, all-optical multiplexer and erbium-doped fiber amplifier (EDFA). Through the simulation, we demonstrate that after adding the noise suppression structure, the system can obtain correct matching results under the same noise environment. For examples, it can correct errors in 16 bit data sequence matching with 8 bit target sequence when the input optical signal-to-noise ratio (OSNR) is between 22dB and 30dB and the noise figure of amplifier is 4dB.

articleTitle: NOMA in Flexible Optical Access Network: Principle, Advantage and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We summarize the current principle, advantage, and challenges of power domain non-orthogonal multiple access technology which exploited the benefits of different channel gains of passive optical network to improve the capacity and achieved flexibility.

articleTitle: Efficient FPGA-based LDPC Encoder Implementation for Optical Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The low-density-parity-code (LDPC) code has been suggested as a forward error correction code in the ITU-T G975.1 protocol for optical communications. However, the traditional LDPC encoding method causes high latency or excessive resource usage, which may degrade the encoder’s throughput and performance. In this paper, we propose an efficient encoder implementation of the LDPC code in the ITU-T G975.1 protocol based on field programmable gate arrays (FPGA). Specifically, the Richardson-Urbanke (RU) algorithm is modified by incorporating the structural characteristics of the parity check matrix that corresponds to the ITU-T G975.1 protocol, along with specific preprocessing techniques. This approach not only simplifies the encoding process but also makes it more suitable for hardware implementation. Our implementation significantly reduces resource consumption and encoding delay compared with existing methods, achieving a throughput of 10Gbps rate.

articleTitle: Meta-learning Accelerated Bi-LSTM for Fiber Nonlinearity Compensation
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Fiber nonlinearity is one of the main limitations for long-reach optical fiber transmissions. We propose a meta-learning accelerated Bi-LSTM algorithm for fiber nonlinearity equalization by saving the training time with different launch powers. The proposed algorithm obtains 0.7 dB Q-factor gain compared to DBP and 81.25% complexity reduction.

articleTitle: Interference Fading Suppression Solution for Phase-sensitive OTDR with Sub Signal Phase Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An interference fading suppression scheme based on phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry ($\Phi$-OTDR) system is proposed. This scheme is based on the energy distribution of sub signals for phase selection. The experimental results show that this scheme has a good effect in suppressing interference fading. The signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the demodulated vibration signal exceeds 35dB. Since this method only processes data in the digital domain without changing the system structure, it does not increase system costs.

articleTitle: Classification and Recognition of Fiber Optic Vibration Sensing Signals Based on Wavelet Packet Decomposition and 1D-CNN Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Algorithm using wavelet packet decomposition and 1D convolutional neural network is proposed to improve recognition accuracy of distributed fiber optic vibration sensor for natural gas pipeline monitoring, achieving average recognition accuracy of >98%.

articleTitle: High-Fidelity and Low-Latency Hollow-Core NANF Transmission at 2-μm Band with 112-Gbps/lambda Data-Rate and 850-m Long Distance
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The 2-μm-band hollow-core NANF transmission is demonstrated with the longest transmission distance of 850m at 56 Gbps and 100m at the highest Intensity-Modulation-Direct-Detection (IMDD) data rate of 112 Gbps by Discrete Multi-Tone (DMT) modulation.

articleTitle: Research on temperature-dependent modulation characteristics of PZT optical fiber phase modulator
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The temperature-dependent modulation characteristics of PZT fiber phase modulator is experimentally investigated. The modulation principle is theoretically analyzed and a Michelson interferometer is constructed to obtain the modulation characteristics in low-temperature range.

articleTitle: Dual-Comb Generation by Recirculating Frequency-Shifting Loop
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Here, we present a new scheme to dual-comb generation based on recirculating frequency-shifting loop. The obtained dual-combs are down-converted to a beat comb with repetition frequencies of 2 MHz.

articleTitle: Nyquist pulse generation based on XPM time lens
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel scheme for generating Nyquist pulses with adjustable duty cycles using time lens based on cross-phase modulation in the high nonlinear fiber is proposed and simulated.

articleTitle: Trajectories and collisions of multiple beams with anomalous vortices in nonlocal materials
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The collision of multiple beams with anomalous vortices in nonlocal materials has been studied in detail. The propagation trajectories of multiple colliding beams have been given, and their dynamic characteristics have been discussed.

articleTitle: Integrated 4-channel wavelength selective switch based on second-order micro-ring resonators
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report a 4-channel wavelength selective switch (WSS) with four second-order micro-ring resonators (MRRs). Each MRR has a flat-top spectrum and are tuned with two micro-heaters. The WSS exhibits a 3dB bandwidth of ~75 GHz and extinction ratios around 10 dB and 22 dB, respectively, at the through and drop ports.

articleTitle: A compact broadband tunable laser source based on REC-DFB laser array
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We develop a compact broadband tunable laser source based on REC-DFB laser array with coverage of 48 nm and adjustable power of 7-10dBm. The wavelength resolution is 2 pm, and power resolution is 0.01 dBm.

articleTitle: High-order mode Brillouin random laser based on distributed Rayleigh scattering in few mode fibers
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A high-order-mode (HOM) Brillouin random fiber laser with an all-few-mode-fiber half-open linear cavity was experimentally demonstrated, highlighting a $610-\text{Hz}$ narrow-linewidth LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode laser emission with high purity of $\sim 91.3 \%$.

articleTitle: Design of a High Speed Directly Modulated Laser with High Output Power
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and design a three-active-section distributed feedback (TAS-DFB) laser utilizing photo-photo resonance to enhance the modulation bandwidth about 55GHz based on optical feedback from an active waveguide, which simultaneously contributes to higher output power.

articleTitle: A Y-Net-aided adaptive compensation for orbital angular momentum optical wireless communication
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive optics (AO) technique based on Y-Net (Y-Net-AO) is proposed to compensate for the distorted OAM beam caused by atmospheric turbulence and to identify the OAM mode number. The Y-Net-aided AO can realize high-precision pattern recognition and distorted OAM beam compensation simultaneously.

articleTitle: pH sensor based on PDMS fiber doped by NaBaScSi2O7: Eu2+
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this study, a pH sensor based on PDMS fiber doped by $\mathrm {NaBaScSi_{2}O_{7}: Eu^{2}}^{+}$ was designed and manufactured. The no-core structured fiber sensor was prepared with fluorescent nanoparticles and silicone-based elastomers that enable both efficient excitation light delivery and fluorescence collection. Upon excitation at 395 nm, the phosphor $\mathrm {NaBaScSi_{2}O_{7}: Eu^{2}}^{+}$ exhibited strong green light peaking at 506 nm. Experimental results showed that the fluorescence intensity of the sensor decreased with the change of the solution in the range of pH 6.86-9.18, and the sensitivity of the sensor was 0.05 /pH. The pH sensor provided the possibility as a technology in biomedical detection and water quality survey and other aspects.

articleTitle: Microstrip Antenna Based on Fractal Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: With the rapid development of communication technology, people increasingly need compact and efficient antennas that can operate at multiple frequencies. However, traditional antenna design methods, such as miniaturization and ultra wideband technology, are often insufficient in meeting the comprehensive requirements of modern communication systems. To address this issue, fractal based antenna design has become a promising solution. This article reviews the research progress of microstrip antennas based on fractal structures in recent years. The simulation results of various fractal based dual frequency microstrip antenna designs were presented, and analysis was conducted from antenna gain, radiation pattern, and other aspects.

articleTitle: Ultra-narrow spectral line Brillouin laser frequency comb
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We combine the principle of four-wave mixing, injection locking and stimulated Brillouin scattering to realize an ultra-narrow spectral line Brillouin laser frequency comb. The linewidth of the optical frequency comb teeth is below 1 Hz.

articleTitle: High spatial resolution temperature sensing based on intensity calculation in RDTS system
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Conventional Raman Distributed Temperature Sensing (RDTS) systems continuously measure multiple regions with a length less than the minimum fiber length required for accurate temperature measurement, the demodulated temperature will have a large error with the true temperature. To obtain high spatial resolution temperature measurements at each region on the sensing fiber, a novel temperature demodulation scheme is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the length of the sensing fiber is divided into multiple regions at equal intervals according to the sampling spacing of data acquisition card, then the relation between temperature and Raman intensity is obtained for each sampling point of temperature rise curve generated by a single region, and the temperature information of each region can be obtained by solving the joint equation finally. The experimental results show that this scheme can improve the spatial resolution of the conventional RDTS system from 4 m to 0.5 m, and the temperature demodulation of five regions with a length of 0.5 m can be realized with a temperature accuracy of ±2.3°C.

articleTitle: Research on Lens-Coupled Dual-Channel Single-Channel Single-Photon Detector System
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Based on optical coupling and free photon counting technology, a lens-coupled dual-channel SPAD singlephoton detector was developed

articleTitle: An improved Lidar point cloud target detection algorithm for networked vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: For the sensing module of assisted driving, 3D point cloud target detection is a crucial technology. To address issues such as slow neural network operation efficiency and low detection accuracy caused by sparse and disordered point cloud data and large data volume, an improved 3D target detection algorithm based on complex-yolo has been proposed. During data processing, raw point cloud data is transformed into a multi-channel bird's-eye view (BEV), followed by feature extraction and fusion on the resulting 2D map. Additionally, to enhance prediction capability, Transformer Prediction Heads (TPH) are utilized in place of original components, which employ self-attention mechanism. Furthermore, the integration of the Convolutional Block Attention Model (CBAM) enables identification of attention regions in scenarios with a high density of objects. In this paper, we use the KITTI dataset to verify and test the algorithm. The results demonstrate an improvement in BEV average precision, which has been improved, which has significant implications for further optimization and improvement of assisted driving technology.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration on ZUC-based Key Expansion for Quantum Noise Stream Cipher
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes a seed key expansion method based on ZUC and bit shifting in QNSC system. Experimental results verify the improved efficiency of key utilization during data encryption, while the security performance is guaranteed.

articleTitle: Real-time Unrepeatered C+L Band Transmission of 36 Tb/s Capacity over 342.5 km
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a record unrepeatered transmission with the capacity of 36 Tb/s ($90\times 400$ Gb/s) over 342.5 km (53.8dB) with C+L band transmission, using forward Raman pump, backward C+L ROPA, and ultra-low loss & large effective area fiber.

articleTitle: Partial and Adaptive Light-Trail Sharing in Multi-Source Multicast Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose flexible multi-source multicast (MSM) grooming in optical networks by allowing MSMs to partially share light-trails and adaptively change the modulation schemes. Simulation results show that the proposed method achieves a better blocking performance.

articleTitle: Enhanced Performance of FAPbBr3-based Inverted Perovskite Light-Emitting Diodes with Amine Additive
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Perovskite is a promising optoelectronic material for various applications including light emitting diodes (LEDs)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1][2]</sup>, due to its high photoluminescence quantum yield and adjustable emission. While progress has been made in optimizing perovskite light-emitting diode (PeLED) efficiency exceeding 20%<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[3]</sup>, research on inverted green PeLEDs remains limited. In this study, we propose an amine additive approach to enhance FAPbBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-based inverted PeLED performance. Our results show that using the amine additive led to compact surface morphology and resulted in PeLED with an enhanced external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 2.8% and maximum luminance of 16000 cd m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>. This study sheds light on the potential of amine-based additive in perovskite optoelectronics, providing a promising strategy for developing high-performance inverted PeLEDs.

articleTitle: High-efficient four-mode Si-SiN interlayer coupler with dual polarizations
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A compact four-mode Si-SiN interlayer coupler with dual polarizations is proposed. The coupler has a low transmission loss of 0.05-0.73 dB and exhibits high fabrication tolerance from 1450 nm to 1650 nm.

articleTitle: Physical Layer Security Enhanced Scheme based on Joint Encryption of Diffusion and Scrambling by Galilean Transformation in CO-OFDM System
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A physical layer encryption scheme is proposed and verified based on joint encryption of diffusion and scrambling by a compound random Galilean transformation in CO-OFDM system. Simulations show that security performance is enhanced with key space of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">180</sup> and PAPR is reduced by 0.8 dB.

articleTitle: Integrated Microwave Photonic Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The emerging microwave photonic (MWP) sensing has demonstrated great promise to offer advanced solutions for cutting-edge applications. The integrated MWP sensors, which use highly sensitive, compact, and CMOS-compatible integrated photonic devices, further push the limits of sensor performance and open up wider potential applications. This paper presents the recent development and advances in MWP sensing with a focus on integrated MWP sensors based on microresonators. An autocorrection-assisted MWP interrogation approach, which can achieve exceptionally high sensing resolution unaffected by the microresonator parameters, is introduced in detail. The first incorporation of machine learning techniques in MWP sensors to enable the temperature insensitive MWP sensing, which uses just a single microring resonance, is also presented.

articleTitle: Data transmission under Smoke pool conditions based on an active mode-locked tunable 2-μm fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a tunable fiber laser in the 2-$\mu \mathrm{m}$ band through active mode-locking and a study of its transmission characteristics in an indoor Smoke pool that simulates atmospheric transport. A segment of 2 m holmium-doped fiber is applied as the gain medium. Actively mode-locked can be realized by introducing periodic intensity modulation into the cavity through a Mach-Zehnder modulator. The nonlinear polarization rotation effect is introduced into the cavity to realize the wavelength tuning range of 2045.31nm~2057.97nm. with optional repetition rates of 1.01 GHz and 2.02 GHz, respectively. After the mode-locked pulse is digitally modulated, it is transmitted in the smoke pool in the laboratory, and the eye diagrams of three different visibility conditions of V=0.5km, 0.05km, and 0.005km are obtained respectively. Compared with the back-to-back condition, the optical signal-to-noise ratio at V=0.005km is reduced by 8.46dB.

articleTitle: Fairness-optimal Resource Allocation Algorithm for NOMA-based Satellite Downlink Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To address the issue of fair resource allocation in low Earth orbit satellite communication systems, a fairness-optimal resource allocation algorithm based on non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) is proposed for satellite downlink systems.

articleTitle: Precise-controlled ultra-high harmonic mode-locking pulses fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The precise-controlled generation of GHz harmonic pulses based on an MZI is reported. Using a fused tapered fiber, we can precisely control the optical path difference of the MZI, thus realizing a precisely controllable repetition rate.

articleTitle: Research on state monitoring of bridge cable based on optical fiber sensing technology
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, the strain and vibration of the bridge cable and its compensation device were monitored using fiber optic grating (FBG) sensing technology on the Zhoushan-Daishan Bridge in Zhoushan, Zhejiang Province. During the monitoring period, the bridge experienced two typhoon events. The strain and vibration signals were analyzed. The results showed that the typhoon 'Muifa' had a greater impact on the Zhoushan-Daishan Bridge than typhoon 'Hinnamnor'. And there was no movement of the expansion compensation device during the monitoring period.

articleTitle: High Sensitive Surface Plasmon Sensor Based on a Simple Nanosystem
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We present a simple nanosystem composed of Ag grating, TiN film and SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> substate, exhibiting a high sensing sensitivity of 1200 nm/RIU with structural simplicity, broadening the application and promoting the development of plasmonic sensors.

articleTitle: Anchor-Damage Event Recognition Based on FBG sensors and CNN-BiLSTM
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The safety monitoring of submarine cables is of increasing concern in the research community. In this study, Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) strain sensors and FBG accelerometer were used to monitor the health status of cables. A method for identifying and localising submarine-cable risk events based on a multi-input Convolutional Neural Networks-Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-BiLSTM) neural network was proposed. The training results of CNN BiLSTM network showed that the total recognition accuracy of the method for eight types of events can reach 97.68%. The results of this study should enrich and improve the theory and methods for identifying and locating submarine-cable risk events and provide support for the development of submarine-cable safety and health-monitoring technology.

articleTitle: Low-Complexity Frequency-Domain MIMO Equalization in Strongly-Coupled Multi-Core Fiber Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a low-complexity frequency-domain MIMO equalization scheme combining unconstrained frequency-domain equalization with out-of-band exclusion. Long-haul strongly-coupled multi-core fiber transmission experiment shows a 73% complexity reduction with negligible performance degradation using the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: A tilted fiber grating humidity sensor based on crystal violet and perfluorosulfonic acid
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Using Etched tilted fiber Bragg grating and coated crystal violet / perfluoric acid composite film, a fiber humidity sensor was developed from 10% to 80% RH with a sensitivity of 0.06 dB/% RH.

articleTitle: Convergence-Efficient Satellite-Ground Federated Learning for LEO Mega Constellations Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose an efficient converged satellite-ground federated learning framework by quickly converging parameters to reduce the training time. Simulation results show that it can improve the global aggregation speed.

articleTitle: Periodically poled lithium niobate-based scheme for optical physical layer security in the coherent optical communications system
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A scheme that can be applied to encrypt and decrypt the signals in the optical physical layer of the coherent optical communications system is proposed and numerically verified. The results show that the scheme can be designed to cause arbitrary ratio of transmission binary code sequence to be misinterpreted by eavesdroppers.

articleTitle: Channel Modeling and Analysis of UAV UV NLOS Communication Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper classifies UAV ultraviolet NLOS communication scenarios and divides them into two types based on whether there are obstacles on the LOS chain. A communication channel model and an uplink and downlink model for each scenario are established, and the height difference between the transmitter and receiver is converted into an angle change, the performance of channel model under different parameter settings is analyzed with Monte Carlo method. The results can guide the actual configuration of communication parameters.

articleTitle: Zn(O,S) Buffer Layer Optimization for CuInGa(S,Se)2 Solar Cells based on Sulfide Nanoparticles Ink
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The mainstream CuInGa(S,Se)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (CIGSSe) solar cells are prepared based on vacuum method and CdS buffer layer. Considering the cost and environmental issues, the preparation of absorber layer based on non-vacuum route with nanoparticle ink and the realization of CdS-free buffer layer is of great importance for large-scale industrialization. Herein, we prepared a Cd-free CIGSSe solar cell with an power conversion efficiency of 6.22% by optimizing the concentration of the reaction solution in chemical bath deposition using a high-quality nanoparticle ink for the absorber layer and Zn(O,S) as the buffer layer; for comparison, the champion CIGSSe solar cell with a PCE of 10.96% based on the CdS buffer layer (without antireflective film).

articleTitle: A Method for Precise Planning of Cerebral Puncture Paths and A 3D Printed Puncture Positioning Device
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Cerebral puncture biopsy is a method of diagnosing and treating cerebral tumors and intracranial hematomas, which has the advantages of low surgical risk, minimal trauma and significant clinical results. In traditional cerebral puncture methods, the surgeon determines the lesion and the scalp entry point through CT scanning and then grasps the angle and depth of the needle based on experience. However, this requires a high level of experience in puncture surgery. In this paper, we propose a method for precise planning of cerebral puncture paths and a 3D-printed puncture positioning device, which simplifies the operational steps without the need for additional instrument-assisted measurement. In the puncture experiment, the total number of punctures was 55 and 49 were successful. The success rate was 89.06%, higher than the success rate of freehand puncture.

articleTitle: Recognition of Object’s Opening Features Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Machine learning is utilized to identify for the objects’ opening number with 100% accuracy. For objects with up to 36 openings, 1° resolution is achieved in all wedge angles and directions with $\gt88.86$% accuracy.

articleTitle: Joint Multi-Layer Proactive Reconstruction for Multi-Domain IP-Optical Integrated Network
publicationTitle: 2023 21st International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A joint multi-layer proactive reconstruction algorithm is proposed to reconstruct IP layer and optical layer simultaneously to adapt to dynamic service requirements for multi-domain IP-optical integrated network, which can effectively reduce blocking probability.
